title: When puberty is late enough to evaluate
lead: Evaluate no breast development by age 13, no menarche by age 15, or no testicular enlargement by age 14.
lines: Those ages start the workup. They are not themselves a diagnosis.
Constitutional delay is a diagnosis of exclusion after the exam, the growth curve, and the indicated labs.
A girl who started breasts and has no period three years later is also late, even if she is not yet 15.
miss: Reassuring a 15-year-old with no periods because a cousin was a late bloomer.
diagramAlt: When to evaluate puberty. Girl: no breast by 13, no menses by 15 Boy: testes under 4 mL at 14 Bone age first. High FSH = gonadal failure

source.name: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 651. Menstruation in Girls and Adolescents: Using the Menstrual Cycle as a Vital Sign (reaffirmed 2025).
source.says: An evaluation for primary amenorrhea should be considered for any adolescent who has not reached menarche by age 15 years or has not done so within 3 years of thelarche. Lack of breast development by age 13 years also should be evaluated.

more.name: StatPearls. Delayed Puberty (boys: no testicular enlargement by age 14).

title: Ambiguous genitalia can be salt-wasting disease
lead: A newborn with atypical genitalia is evaluated for salt-wasting congenital adrenal hyperplasia before the baby goes home.
lines: A virilized or atypical newborn is evaluated for 21-hydroxylase deficiency before anyone assigns a sex or sends the infant home.
Salt-wasting disease is part of that guideline's clinical management, not a reassurance visit.
The infant who is ill is treated, not observed until a karyotype result returns.
In weeks 1 to 3 the sodium falls and the potassium rises, often above 6. 17-hydroxyprogesterone is very high. Give hydrocortisone and saline, then fludrocortisone.
miss: Discharging a virilized newborn with no plan for salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency.
diagramAlt: Salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase. Week 1–3: Na low, K over 6 17-hydroxyprogesterone very high Hydrocortisone + saline, then fludrocortisone

source.name: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia Due to Steroid 21-Hydroxylase Deficiency.
source.says: Missed diagnosis of salt-losing CAH is associated with increased risk for early neonatal morbidity and mortality. 4.3 In the newborn and in early infancy, we recommend using fludrocortisone and sodium chloride supplements to the treatment regimen.

title: Turner syndrome is followed for the aorta and the growth
lead: A girl with Turner syndrome gets blood-pressure checks, aortic imaging, and a growth conversation. The karyotype is not the end of the visit.
lines: Coarctation and a bicuspid valve are what you listen and image for.
The kidneys are imaged once.
Estrogen is replaced at the time of puberty, with a specialist, because the streak gonads will not produce it.
miss: Measuring height once and never taking a blood pressure in the legs.

source.name: Clinical practice guidelines for the care of girls and women with Turner syndrome (International Turner Syndrome Consensus Group).
source.says: R 4.7: TTE should be performed at the time of diagnosis in all children and adults with TS. R 4.17: annual assessment of blood pressure for all individuals with TS. R 7.21: a renal ultrasound at time of diagnosis. R 3.2: low dose estrogen replacement between 11 and 12 years of age, if FSH is elevated.

title: Klinefelter syndrome is treated as hypogonadism
lead: Men with Klinefelter syndrome and low testosterone are offered testosterone replacement. The infertility is a separate conversation and is not fixed by the gel.
lines: Breast tissue is examined because the cancer risk is higher.
Learning differences are supported. They are not the reason to withhold hormone treatment.
Testosterone treats the hypogonadism. It does not restore sperm. Breast cancer risk is higher than in other men.
Small firm testes, tall stature, azoospermia, and gynecomastia. Testosterone is low and LH and FSH are high.
miss: Telling the patient testosterone will restore sperm.

source.name: StatPearls. Klinefelter Syndrome.
source.says: Initiating testosterone replacement early remains the cornerstone of treatment. In some cases, assisted reproductive technologies can restore fertility. Individuals with Klinefelter syndrome are at increased risk for complications such as osteoporosis, metabolic syndrome, breast cancer, and autoimmune disorders.

title: DiGeorge is calcium, infection, and the heart
lead: A newborn with DiGeorge features gets a calcium, an immune evaluation, and a heart evaluation. The low calcium can be the first seizure.
lines: Irradiated blood is used if a transfusion is needed and the immune defect is not yet clear.
Live vaccines wait until the immune status is known.
The face and the outflow murmur are the clues to order those tests.
Third pouch: inferior parathyroids and thymus. Fourth pouch: superior parathyroids.
Ionized calcium can fall in the first days of life. A neonatal seizure here is hypocalcemia until the lab returns.
miss: Treating a neonatal seizure with an antiseizure drug and never checking the calcium.

source.name: StatPearls. DiGeorge Syndrome.
source.says: Hypoparathyroidism manifests as hypocalcemia ranging from neonatal seizures and tetany to subclinical hypocalcemia. Cardiovascular evaluation includes echocardiography in all newly diagnosed patients. Complete DiGeorge syndrome requires irradiated leukocyte-reduced CMV-negative blood products only and no live attenuated vaccines.

title: TTP is not a platelet order
lead: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is a medical emergency treated with plasma exchange. Platelets are for life-threatening bleeding, not for the number.
lines: High clinical suspicion: draw ADAMTS13 before any plasma exchange or blood product.
Then start therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids without waiting for the ADAMTS13 result.
The ISTH treatment guideline strongly recommends adding corticosteroids to plasma exchange for a first episode or a relapse.
Caplacizumab is a conditional addition in the treatment guideline. It is not a reason to delay plasma exchange.
miss: Waiting for the ADAMTS13 result before plasma exchange when the clinical suspicion is already high.
diagramAlt: TTP versus ITP. TTP: schistocytes, hemolysis, exchange now ITP: isolated low platelets, no fragments Platelets in TTP only for life-threatening bleed

source.name: ISTH guidelines for the diagnosis of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.
source.says: If the pretest probability of TTP is high, start TPE and corticosteroids, and collect plasma samples for ADAMTS13 testing before therapy. Acquire a plasma sample for ADAMTS13 testing before an initiation of TPE or use of any blood product.

title: Febrile neutropenia does not wait for the culture
lead: Fever with an absolute neutrophil count under 500 needs an antipseudomonal antibiotic within an hour of recognition.
lines: Fever plus neutropenia is treated at once with broad empiric antibiotics. Do not wait for a culture to grow.
The IDSA 2010 update states that immediate empiric therapy has not changed: cover gram-positive and gram-negative pathogens.
Risk stratification decides the setting. It does not delay the first dose.
A narrow oral drug chosen before that first broad dose is the miss.
miss: Waiting for the culture result before the first broad antibiotic dose.

source.name: ASCO/IDSA Clinical Practice Guideline Update. Outpatient Management of Fever and Neutropenia in Adults Treated for Malignancy.
source.says: Patients with febrile neutropenia receive initial doses of empirical antibacterial therapy within 1 hour of triage. Monotherapy with an antipseudomonal β-lactam agent, such as cefepime, a carbapenem, or piperacillin-tazobactam, is recommended (endorsed from the 2010 IDSA guideline).

more.name: IDSA 2010 update. Antimicrobial agents in neutropenic patients with cancer.

title: Acute chest syndrome is more than pain medicine
lead: Acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease is a new infiltrate with chest pain, fever, or hypoxia. Incentive spirometry prevents it, and severe disease is an exchange-transfusion conversation.
lines: Antibiotics cover community pneumonia while you treat the sickle crisis.
Simple transfusion is for a drop in hemoglobin. Exchange is for the severe respiratory failure.
Pain control that lets the patient take deep breaths is part of the prevention.
Exchange transfusion for severe acute chest or acute stroke. Simple transfusion is for symptomatic anemia. Hydroxyurea is prevention, not today's stroke drug.
miss: Discharging a hypoxic sickle-cell patient with oral opioids and no film.

source.name: NHLBI Expert Panel Report. Evidence-Based Management of Sickle Cell Disease.
source.says: To reduce the risk of acute chest syndrome in adults and children hospitalized for a VOC, encourage use of incentive spirometry while awake. Perform urgent exchange transfusion when there is rapid progression of ACS, such as oxygen saturation below 90 percent despite supplemental oxygen.

more.name: BSH guideline on acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease (2015).

title: Bleeding ITP is treated. A number alone may not be
lead: Immune thrombocytopenia is treated when there is bleeding or a procedure, not because every low number must be normalized today.
lines: ASH lists observation as a way to manage immune thrombocytopenia when bleeding is not forcing treatment.
When treatment is chosen, corticosteroids are one of the approaches the guideline considers.
The panel favored options that avoid drug toxicity for non–life-threatening bleeding.
Approaches named in the guideline also include IVIG, anti-D immunoglobulin, rituximab, splenectomy, and thrombopoietin receptor agonists.
miss: Transfusing platelets for a number, in a patient who is not bleeding, as the treatment of immune thrombocytopenia.
diagramAlt: TTP versus ITP. TTP: schistocytes, hemolysis, exchange now ITP: isolated low platelets, no fragments Platelets in TTP only for life-threatening bleed

source.name: ASH 2019 guidelines for immune thrombocytopenia.
source.says: In adults with newly diagnosed ITP and a platelet count of ≥30 × 10^9/L who are asymptomatic or have minor mucocutaneous bleeding, the ASH guideline panel recommends against corticosteroids and in favor of management with observation.

title: A hemophilia bleed gets factor, not fresh frozen plasma as the plan
lead: A joint or muscle bleed in hemophilia A is treated with factor VIII replacement. Fresh frozen plasma is not the outpatient plan.
lines: A mixing study that no longer corrects means an inhibitor.
Avoid intramuscular injections and NSAIDs.
PT is normal. PTT is long and corrects with mixing unless an inhibitor has formed.
miss: Sending a hemarthrosis home on ibuprofen.

source.name: WFH Guidelines for the Management of Hemophilia, 3rd edition.
source.says: Hemophilia patients with severe hemarthrosis should be treated immediately with intravenous clotting factor concentrate replacement until there is bleed resolution. For patients with hemophilia, fresh frozen plasma is not recommended. NSAIDs (except selective COX-2 inhibitors) should not be used.

title: Desmopressin is for type 1 von Willebrand, not type 2B
lead: Type 1 von Willebrand disease can be treated with desmopressin before a procedure. Type 2B can worsen because the abnormal multimer binds platelets.
lines: Know the subtype before the drug.
Antifibrinolytics help mucosal bleeding.
Factor replacement that contains von Willebrand factor is the alternative when desmopressin is unsafe.
vWF carries factor VIII. Mucosal bleeding with a normal platelet count is the picture. PTT prolongs only if VIII is low.
miss: Giving desmopressin to every patient with the disease name and watching the platelet count fall.
diagramAlt: Desmopressin in VWD. Type 1: desmopressin often works Type 2B: desmopressin can drop platelets Mucosal bleeding. PTT may be normal

source.name: ASH ISTH NHF WFH 2021 guidelines on the management of von Willebrand disease.
source.says: In patients for whom desmopressin is a valid treatment option (primarily type 1 VWD), the panel suggests performing a trial of desmopressin. Desmopressin is contraindicated in type 2B VWD because of increased platelet binding with subsequent thrombocytopenia.

title: DIC is treated by treating the cause
lead: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is treated by treating the cause. Blood products are for bleeding or a procedure, not for a daily number.
lines: Treat the underlying condition. That is the cornerstone of DIC treatment in the ISTH harmonized guidance.
Transfuse platelets or plasma only for a patient who is bleeding, not for a number alone.
If thrombosis is the dominant picture, consider a therapeutic dose of heparin. Do not use that dose when bleeding risk is high.
Critically ill patients who are not bleeding should receive prophylactic unfractionated or low-molecular-weight heparin.
miss: Treating a laboratory number with plasma while the cause of the DIC is left untreated.
diagramAlt: DIC labs. Low fibrinogen, high D-dimer PT and PTT both prolong Cryoprecipitate if bleeding and fibrinogen is low

source.name: ISTH SSC guidance. Diagnosis and treatment of DIC, harmonized from three guidelines.
source.says: The cornerstone of DIC treatment is the treatment of the underlying condition. In general, transfusion of platelets or plasma (components) in patients with DIC should be reserved for patients who are bleeding. Prophylactic doses of unfractionated heparin or low molecular weight heparin is recommended in critically ill and non-bleeding patients with DIC.

title: Do not start warfarin alone for HIT
lead: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is treated by stopping all heparin and starting a non-heparin anticoagulant. Warfarin alone is dangerous in the acute phase.
lines: Estimate probability with the 4Ts score, not a gestalt impression.
A low-probability 4Ts score is not an indication to stop heparin and start another anticoagulant.
An intermediate or high score: stop heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant. ASH names argatroban, bivalirudin, danaparoid, fondaparinux, and a direct oral anticoagulant.
Do not start warfarin before the platelet count recovers, usually to at least 150 × 10^9/L. Early warfarin is linked to venous limb gangrene.
miss: Stopping heparin without a non-heparin anticoagulant when the 4Ts score is intermediate or high, or starting warfarin while the platelet count is still low.
diagramAlt: HIT, day 5 to 10. Platelets fall >=50% at day 5-10 With or without thrombosis Stop heparin. No warfarin before recovery

source.name: ASH 2018 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
source.says: Strong recommendations include use of the 4Ts score rather than a gestalt approach and avoidance of empiric treatment of HIT with a low-probability 4Ts score. The panel suggests argatroban, bivalirudin, danaparoid, fondaparinux, or a DOAC, and recommends against a VKA before platelet count recovery (usually ≥150 × 10^9/L).

title: Established tumor lysis with a high uric acid gets rasburicase
lead: Allopurinol prevents new uric acid. Rasburicase breaks down uric acid that is already there. A high uric acid with tumor lysis gets rasburicase if it is available.
lines: Fluids are started in everyone at risk.
Screen for G6PD deficiency before rasburicase when you can. The drug can hemolyze those patients.
The potassium is the immediate threat on the monitor.
Potassium and phosphate and uric acid rise. Calcium falls.
miss: Starting only allopurinol when the uric acid is already 14 and the potassium is 6.
diagramAlt: Tumor lysis ions. K up, phosphate up, uric acid up Calcium down (binds phosphate) Rasburicase clears uric acid already made

source.name: British Society for Haematology updated guidelines for the diagnosis and management of tumour lysis syndrome in adults and children with haematological malignancies.
source.says: Patients with established TLS should be treated with rasburicase 0.2 mg/kg/day. Allopurinol should be stopped when rasburicase is commenced. Patients who may receive rasburicase should be tested for G6PD deficiency, as rasburicase can cause haemolytic anaemia or methaemoglobinaemia. Patients with TLS should have vigorous intravenous hydration.

title: Phlebotomy is the treatment of polycythemia vera
lead: Polycythemia vera is treated by phlebotomy to lower the hematocrit, plus aspirin when the diagnosis is secure and the platelets are not extreme.
lines: A high erythropoietin is not this disease. Do not phlebotomize hypoxic lung disease down to an unsafe hematocrit.
Hydroxyurea is added for high-risk patients.
Aquagenic itching is a clue, not a dermatology referral alone.
A high EPO is secondary erythrocytosis.
Do not apply that target to hypoxic lung disease.
miss: Phlebotomizing a patient with a high EPO from lung disease to a hematocrit of 40.
diagramAlt: Polycythemia vera target. JAK2. EPO is low Phlebotomy toward hematocrit <45% Do not phlebotomize hypoxic high-EPO disease

source.name: ELN revised management recommendations for Philadelphia chromosome-negative classical myeloproliferative neoplasms.
source.says: The Panel strongly recommended that all patients with PV should be managed with phlebotomy to maintain the hematocrit below 45%, together with daily low-dose acetyl salicylic acid.

title: Start ATRA when the smear says promyelocytic leukemia
lead: Acute promyelocytic leukemia is treated with all-trans retinoic acid as soon as the diagnosis is suspected. Do not wait for the karyotype if the smear and the coagulopathy match.
lines: The early death is bleeding. Correct the coagulopathy.
Differentiation syndrome is fever and pulmonary infiltrates after the drug starts. It is treated, not ignored.
Auer rods and a bilobed nucleus are the smear. The translocation is between chromosomes 15 and 17.
miss: Waiting three days for cytogenetics while the fibrinogen falls.
diagramAlt: APL, do not wait. Auer rods. t(15;17) ATRA when the smear fits Bleeding is the early death. Follow fibrinogen

source.name: ELN expert-panel recommendations for the management of acute promyelocytic leukemia.
source.says: ATRA should be initiated immediately once APL is suspected. Transfusions of fibrinogen and/or cryoprecipitate, platelets, and fresh-frozen plasma should be given to maintain the fibrinogen concentration above 100 to 150 mg/dL and the platelet count above 30 to 50 × 10^9/L.

title: PNH with hemolysis or thrombosis gets a complement inhibitor
lead: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria with hemolysis or thrombosis is treated with a complement inhibitor. Anticoagulation alone does not stop the complement.
lines: Unusual-site thrombosis is this disease until the flow cytometry is back.
Iron is lost in the urine. Replace it if the patient is deficient. Do not assume the anemia is iron overload.
Eculizumab raises the Neisseria risk. Vaccinate.
miss: Anticoagulating a hepatic-vein thrombosis and never ordering the flow cytometry.

source.name: StatPearls. Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria.
source.says: Advances in treatment such as the development of eculizumab have improved survival to more than 75 percent, and ravulizumab will likely replace eculizumab as the first-line treatment for PNH.

title: A hemolytic transfusion reaction stops the unit
lead: Fever, pain, or dark urine during a transfusion stops that unit. Do not slow it and watch.
lines: Check the identity of the patient and the bag. Clerical error is the classic cause.
Support the pressure and the urine output.
A febrile nonhemolytic reaction is a diagnosis you make after hemolysis is unlikely, not before you stop the blood.
ABO mismatch causes fever, flank pain, and hemoglobinuria during the transfusion. Stop that unit.
Keep the bag. Send it back with a fresh sample. Clerical error is the usual cause. Do not restart the same unit.
miss: Restarting the same unit after acetaminophen.

source.name: BSH Guideline on the investigation and management of acute transfusion reactions.
source.says: If a patient develops new symptoms or signs during a transfusion, this should be stopped temporarily but venous access should be maintained, and identification details checked against the component. If febrile symptoms are sustained, a haemolytic reaction should be considered, the unit returned, and samples taken for repeat compatibility testing.

title: Either thrombolytic, inside 4.5 hours
lead: For an eligible adult within 4.5 hours, give tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg up to 25 mg, or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg up to 90 mg.
lines: Disabling deficit is the indication. A low NIHSS score does not cancel it.
Do not use advanced imaging to withhold treatment inside 4.5 hours.
Tenecteplase 0.4 mg/kg is not the dose in this window.
Check glucose and a noncontrast CT first. Hypoglycemia copies a stroke and is not treated with a thrombolytic.
miss: Waiting for an MRI, or quoting only alteplase, in a patient who is already inside the window.
diagramAlt: Inside 4.5 hours, tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg up to 25 mg or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg up to 90 mg. Blood pressure before treatment is below 185 over 110.

source.name: 2026 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke.
source.says: The guideline endorses either alteplase or tenecteplase in the 4.5-hour window: tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg); a 0.4 mg/kg tenecteplase dose is not recommended. Disabling deficits are treated regardless of NIHSS score, without advanced imaging selection; BP is brought below 185/110 first.

title: Status epilepticus: benzodiazepine first
lead: A seizure that continues, or that recurs without recovery, gets a benzodiazepine now. The second drug is not another benzodiazepine.
lines: Give IV lorazepam, or IM midazolam if there is no IV.
If it continues, give one adequate dose of fosphenytoin, valproate, or levetiracetam. Those three are equivalent as the next drug.
Do not stack small benzodiazepine doses and call that treatment.
Check glucose, then give a benzodiazepine: intravenous lorazepam or intramuscular midazolam if there is no line.

If the seizure continues, give one full dose of levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4500 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg/kg (max 1500 mg), or valproate 40 mg/kg (max 3000 mg). ESETT found them equivalent. Do not stack quarter-doses.
miss: Starting a phenytoin load while the first benzodiazepine dose was never given.
diagramAlt: Status epilepticus drugs. Glucose, then a benzodiazepine Then one full second drug Levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, or valproate

source.name: AES Evidence-Based Guideline: Treatment of Convulsive Status Epilepticus in Children and Adults.
source.says: A benzodiazepine (specifically IM midazolam, IV lorazepam, or IV diazepam) is recommended as the initial therapy of choice (level A). Compared to the first therapy, the second therapy is less effective (level A).

more.name: Kapur et al. ESETT: levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, and valproate for benzodiazepine-refractory status epilepticus. NEJM 2019.

title: Thunderclap headache is a bleed until it is not
lead: A headache that is maximal at onset gets a noncontrast head CT now. A negative CT is enough only within 6 hours of onset with no new deficit.
lines: Do the CT before the neurology consult and before a migraine cocktail.
If the CT is negative after 6 hours, or there is a new deficit, the next test is lumbar puncture or a vascular study, based on timing and availability.
Exertion, pregnancy, a focal deficit, fever with neck stiffness, cancer, or immunosuppression also moves imaging up. A stable recurrent migraine does not.
miss: Sending the patient home because the CT was read overnight as negative and nobody asked how the headache started.

source.name: 2023 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
source.says: Noncontrast head CT remains the mainstay of SAH diagnosis. For patients presenting within 6 hours of headache onset who have no new neurological deficits, the lack of SAH on a noncontrast head CT is likely sufficient to exclude aSAH; otherwise LP for xanthochromia or CTA is the next study after a negative or nondiagnostic CT.

title: Dexamethasone before the meningitis antibiotic
lead: In adults with suspected pneumococcal meningitis, give dexamethasone before or with the first antibiotic dose.
lines: The point is to blunt the inflammatory burst as bacteria lyse. After the antibiotic is already in, the window is gone.
Do not delay the antibiotic for a CT if there is no indication for CT. Blood cultures, then drug, then the puncture if imaging has to come first.
Stop the steroid if the organism is not Streptococcus pneumoniae, unless another indication exists.
miss: Hanging the antibiotic, then remembering the steroid an hour later.

source.name: NICE guideline NG240. Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management.
source.says: For people over 3 months with strongly suspected or confirmed bacterial meningitis, give intravenous dexamethasone, with the first dose with or before the first dose of antibiotics if possible. Continue dexamethasone if the organism is pneumococcus or Haemophilus influenzae type b; stop dexamethasone for all other organisms.

more.name: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Management of Bacterial Meningitis (2004, archived).

title: Guillain-Barré is IVIG or exchange, not prednisone
lead: Guillain-Barré syndrome is treated with intravenous immunoglobulin or plasma exchange. Steroids do not help.
lines: IVIg 0.4 g/kg daily for 5 days if the patient cannot walk unaided and weakness began within 2 weeks. A good-practice point also allows 2 to 4 weeks.
Or plasma exchange, 12–15 L in four to five exchanges over 1 to 2 weeks, if weakness began within 4 weeks and the patient cannot walk unaided.
Do not use oral corticosteroids. A second course of IVIg for a poor prognosis is recommended against.
Use the modified Erasmus GBS Respiratory Insufficiency Score for the ventilation risk. CSF examination is valuable when the diagnosis is uncertain.
miss: Starting prednisone, or quoting a vital-capacity cutoff this guideline does not use, instead of IVIg or plasma exchange.
diagramAlt: Guillain-Barré breathing. IVIG or exchange. Not prednisone Vital capacity under 20 mL/kg: intubate window CSF: high protein, almost no cells

source.name: EAN/PNS guideline on diagnosis and treatment of Guillain-Barré syndrome.
source.says: The task force recommends IVIg 0.4 g/kg for 5 days within 2 weeks (GPP also within 2-4 weeks) after onset of weakness if unable to walk unaided, or plasma exchange 12-15 L in four to five exchanges over 1-2 weeks within 4 weeks; it recommends against oral corticosteroids and advises the mEGRIS score for ventilation risk.

title: An acute multiple-sclerosis flare gets a steroid, not an antibiotic
lead: A new disabling multiple-sclerosis flare is treated with high-dose corticosteroids. An antibiotic does not treat a demyelinating plaque.
lines: Infection can worsen old symptoms without a new plaque. Look for it before you call every worsening a flare.
Disease-modifying therapy is the long plan and is not the same syringe as the flare steroid.
Optic neuritis is this conversation, and vision is followed.
Dissemination in time and space, plus unmatched oligoclonal bands. One lesion is not the disease.
A new disabling deficit can get high-dose steroids. The same old deficit plus a fever is infection until proved otherwise.
miss: Giving antibiotics for a sensory level and a clear urine.
diagramAlt: MS flare versus infection. New deficit: high-dose steroid Old deficit plus fever: find the infection Disease-modifying drug is a separate order

source.name: NICE guideline NG220. Multiple sclerosis in adults: management.
source.says: Assess and offer treatment for relapses of MS that affect the person's ability to perform their usual tasks as early as possible and within 14 days of onset. Offer treatment for relapse of MS with oral methylprednisolone 0.5 g daily for 5 days. Not all relapses need treating with steroids.

title: Levodopa is the most effective drug for Parkinson motor symptoms
lead: When Parkinson disease limits function, levodopa is the most effective drug for the motor symptoms. Saving it for late disease is an old idea.
lines: Carbidopa is given with it so less is lost in the periphery.
A dopamine blocker on the medication list is stopped before the diagnosis is locked.
Impulse-control problems are the agonist story. Ask about gambling and sex.
Rest tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia from nigral dopamine loss. Give hospital doses at the home clock times.
miss: Withholding levodopa for years from a patient who can no longer walk, out of fear of it wearing off.
diagramAlt: Parkinson doses in hospital. Give carbidopa-levodopa at home times No metoclopramide or haloperidol Levodopa is the strongest motor drug

source.name: AAN practice guideline summary. Dopaminergic therapy for motor symptoms in early Parkinson disease.
source.says: In patients with early PD who seek treatment for motor symptoms, clinicians should recommend levodopa as the initial preferential dopaminergic therapy (Level B). Clinical trials have failed to provide evidence of disease modification when the initial therapy is levodopa, a DA, or an MAO-B inhibitor.

title: Absence epilepsy is ethosuximide
lead: Ethosuximide is the drug for childhood absence seizures. Carbamazepine can worsen them.
lines: There is no postictal confusion. A confused child had a different seizure.
Hyperventilation can reproduce the spell in the office.
A child who also has generalized convulsions needs a drug that covers both, which ethosuximide does not.
Ethosuximide if this is the only seizure type.
miss: Starting carbamazepine for staring spells.
diagramAlt: Absence drug. 3 Hz spike-and-wave. No postictal state Ethosuximide if absence is the only seizure Carbamazepine can worsen pure absence

source.name: NICE guideline NG217. Epilepsies in children, young people and adults (5.3 Absence seizures).
source.says: Offer ethosuximide as first-line treatment for absence seizures (including childhood absence epilepsy). Be aware that carbamazepine, gabapentin, oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, pregabalin, tiagabine and vigabatrin may exacerbate seizures in people with absence seizures.

title: Carbamazepine is first for trigeminal neuralgia
lead: Trigeminal neuralgia is treated with carbamazepine. A dental extraction is not the treatment of electric pain.
lines: The shock lasts under 2 minutes, in one trigeminal division, and is triggered by touch, chewing, or a breeze.
Carbamazepine is first-line. Check sodium. A spreading rash can be Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and the drug stops.
Oxcarbazepine is the usual alternative. A dental extraction does not treat the nerve.
miss: Pulling a tooth for seconds of shock-like pain in the cheek.
diagramAlt: Trigeminal neuralgia. Seconds of shock in one branch Carbamazepine first Check sodium. Young or numb: image

source.name: AAN/EFNS practice parameter. Diagnostic evaluation and treatment of trigeminal neuralgia.
source.says: Carbamazepine (Level A) or oxcarbazepine (Level B) should be offered for pain control in trigeminal neuralgia, while baclofen and lamotrigine (Level C) may be considered useful.

title: Stop the antipsychotic in neuroleptic malignant syndrome
lead: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is treated by stopping the dopamine blocker, cooling, and supporting the pressure. Another dose of the same drug is not the treatment of the agitation.
lines: Creatine kinase is high and the reflexes are not clonus.
A benzodiazepine can help agitation. The antipsychotic does not.
Restarting a drug later, if ever, is a specialist decision at a low dose.
Lead-pipe rigidity and high CK over days. Reflexes are reduced, not clonic.
miss: Increasing the antipsychotic because the patient is more confused.
diagramAlt: NMS versus serotonin syndrome. NMS: lead-pipe, high CK, days Serotonin: clonus, hours, two drugs Stop the offending drug in both

source.name: StatPearls. Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
source.says: Treatment involves immediately discontinuing the offending agent, aggressive supportive care to manage and prevent complications, and pharmacologic therapy in severe cases. The empiric medications most frequently used for refractory NMS include bromocriptine and dantrolene.

title: Stop the serotonergic drugs
lead: Serotonin syndrome is treated by stopping the serotonergic drugs and giving a benzodiazepine for agitation. Cyproheptadine is the antidote when supportive care is not enough.
lines: Clonus is the sign that separates it from neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
It starts in hours, so today's new prescription is the cause.
Clonus and hyperreflexia within hours of an SSRI plus an MAOI, linezolid, tramadol, or a triptan. Stop both drugs on that shift.
A benzodiazepine treats the agitation. Cyproheptadine is the antagonist if support is not enough. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is rigidity over days, not clonus.
miss: Adding linezolid to an SSRI and treating the shivering as influenza.
diagramAlt: NMS versus serotonin syndrome. NMS: lead-pipe, high CK, days Serotonin: clonus, hours, two drugs Stop the offending drug in both

source.name: StatPearls. Serotonin Syndrome.
source.says: Treatment for serotonin syndrome involves discontinuing the offending medications and providing supportive care. Benzodiazepines are the preferred agents for agitation. If supportive measures and chemical sedation do not adequately treat serotonin syndrome, antidotes (serotonin antagonists such as cyproheptadine) can be considered the next step.

title: A high lithium level is held, and severe toxicity is dialyzed
lead: Hold lithium and check the level when tremor, confusion, or a drug interaction appears. Severe neurotoxicity or a very high level is dialyzed.
lines: Hold lithium when toxicity is suspected and send a level timed after distribution, not in the first hours.
EXTRIP recommends extracorporeal treatment for severe lithium poisoning.
Intravenous saline treats volume loss. It does not replace dialysis when neurotoxicity is severe.
Chronic use can cause nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. That is a different problem from one toxic level.
miss: Treating severe lithium neurotoxicity with saline alone.
diagramAlt: Lithium interactions. NSAIDs, thiazides, ACE inhibitors raise it Hold the drug. Severe toxicity: dialysis Chronic use: nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

source.name: EXTRIP. Extracorporeal Treatment for Lithium Poisoning: Systematic Review and Recommendations.
source.says: Extracorporeal treatment is recommended in severe lithium poisoning: if kidney function is impaired and the [Li+] is >4.0 mEq/L, or with a decreased level of consciousness, seizures, or life-threatening dysrhythmias irrespective of the [Li+]. It is suggested if the [Li+] is >5.0 mEq/L or significant confusion is present.

title: Do not treat tardive dyskinesia with a higher dose as the plan
lead: Tardive dyskinesia is managed by reassessing the antipsychotic, not by raising a first-generation drug. A VMAT2 inhibitor is the specific treatment.
lines: Acute dystonia is the opposite time course and answers to an anticholinergic.
The movements can persist after the drug stops. Warn the patient.
Akathisia is restlessness and is a different dose change.
Acute dystonia is hours and responds to benztropine.
miss: Doubling haloperidol for mouth movements that started after a year of haloperidol.

source.name: StatPearls. Tardive Dyskinesia.
source.says: Vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) inhibitors represent the most significant therapeutic advancement in tardive dyskinesia; valbenazine demonstrates sustained improvement in symptoms with once-daily dosing.

title: Bell palsy gets a steroid early and eye protection
lead: Idiopathic Bell palsy is treated with oral corticosteroids within the first few days. The eye that does not close is lubricated.
lines: Oral corticosteroids are strongly recommended within 72 hours of onset of peripheral facial nerve palsy.
Antivirals may be added. They are not a substitute for the corticosteroid.
Routine testing is unnecessary for a typical presentation. Atypical features are the reason to test further.
The 2026 facial-nerve-palsy guideline is the source for that 72-hour corticosteroid recommendation.
miss: Starting an antiviral without a corticosteroid, or starting the corticosteroid after 72 hours as if the window were still open.
diagramAlt: Bell palsy, first 72 hours. Forehead involved = peripheral nerve Prednisone early. Lubricate the eye Forehead spared = stroke pathway

source.name: Clinical practice guideline for the evaluation and management of peripheral facial nerve palsy (Korean multidisciplinary guideline).
source.says: Oral corticosteroids are strongly recommended within 72 hours of symptom onset (Grade A). Antivirals may be added based on clinical judgment and patient preference (Grade B). Routine testing is unnecessary for typical Bell's palsy; selective testing is advised for atypical features.

title: A deteriorating epidural hematoma goes to surgery
lead: An epidural hematoma in a patient who is worsening goes to surgical evacuation. The lucid interval is the time you still have.
lines: An epidural hematoma larger than 30 mL is evacuated, whatever the Glasgow Coma Scale score.
A patient who was talking and is now worsening does not wait for the next scheduled scan.
Reverse anticoagulation and send a type and screen on the way to the operating room.
The blood is lens-shaped and does not cross sutures. That shape is the middle meningeal artery.
miss: Watching an epidural hematoma over 30 mL because the patient is still speaking.

source.name: Brain Trauma Foundation. Surgical management of acute epidural hematomas.
source.says: An epidural hematoma (EDH) greater than 30 cm3 should be surgically evacuated regardless of the patient's Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score.

title: A large or symptomatic subdural hematoma is surgical
lead: A subdural hematoma that shifts the brain or worsens the exam is evacuated. Anticoagulation is reversed.
lines: Older patients can have a large collection and a mild first complaint. The scan decides the size.
A small chronic collection without mass effect can be followed.
Do not restart the anticoagulant the same evening without a plan.
Bridging veins, crescent, crosses sutures. Atrophy and anticoagulation are the setup.
Symptoms can be days after a minor fall. Reverse anticoagulation if the collection is symptomatic or shifting.
miss: Restarting warfarin the night of the fall because the patient has atrial fibrillation and the CT was not yet done.

source.name: Brain Trauma Foundation. Surgical management of acute subdural hematomas.
source.says: An acute subdural hematoma (SDH) with a thickness greater than 10 mm or a midline shift greater than 5 mm on CT scan should be surgically evacuated, regardless of the patient's GCS score, and as soon as possible.

title: Cerebellar hemorrhage is a surgical conversation
lead: A cerebellar hemorrhage that compresses the brainstem or blocks the ventricle is evacuated. Do not watch it on the floor.
lines: The signs are headache, vomiting, and ataxia, then a falling level of consciousness.
Blood pressure is lowered into the range the hemorrhagic-stroke guidance uses, without dropping perfusion.
A deep small bleed in the putamen is a different surgical decision from the cerebellum.
Putamen, thalamus, pons, and cerebellum are the hypertensive sites. Lobar hemorrhage in older adults is amyloid until proved otherwise.
miss: Waiting for the patient to become comatose before calling neurosurgery.
diagramAlt: Which bleed goes to surgery. Cerebellum with compression: evacuate Putamen: usually medical Lobar in an older adult: think amyloid

source.name: 2022 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
source.says: For patients with cerebellar hemorrhage, indications for immediate surgical evacuation with or without an external ventricular drain to reduce mortality include larger volume (>15 mL) in addition to neurological deterioration, brainstem compression, and hydrocephalus.

title: Triptan overuse is 10 or more days a month
lead: A triptan treats migraine early. It is contraindicated in coronary disease, uncontrolled hypertension, and with recent ergot or another triptan.
lines: Headache on 15 or more days a month, for more than 3 months, in someone with a prior headache disorder, is the ICHD-3 frame for medication-overuse headache.
Triptans, ergots, opioids, and combination analgesics meet overuse at 10 or more days a month.
The treatment implied by the diagnosis is to stop the overused acute drug, not to raise the monthly count.
miss: Refilling a near-daily triptan or combination analgesic without counting the days per month.

source.name: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (ICHD-3). 8.2.2 Triptan-overuse headache.
source.says: Triptan-overuse headache is headache occurring on 15 or more days/month in a patient with a pre-existing primary headache, developing as a consequence of regular use of one or more triptans on 10 or more days/month for more than 3 months.

title: Stop the anticholinergic in a patient with dementia
lead: Anticholinergic drugs worsen Alzheimer disease. A cholinesterase inhibitor is a modest symptomatic drug, not a cure, and it fights the anticholinergic.
lines: A sudden confusion is delirium until the cause is found. It is not a dose increase of the dementia drug.
Frontotemporal change is a different disease and does not answer to the same drug.
Caregiver support and safety are the treatment that matters as much as the pill.
Diphenhydramine and other strong anticholinergics worsen cognition and are on the Beers list. Stop them rather than adding a cholinesterase inhibitor on top.
miss: Adding diphenhydramine for sleep in a patient who is already losing memory.
diagramAlt: Beers drugs that cause admissions. Benzodiazepines for sleep or anxiety Strong anticholinergics, including diphenhydramine Sliding-scale insulin used alone

source.name: American Geriatrics Society 2023 Updated AGS Beers Criteria for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults.
source.says: Drug-disease interaction: in dementia or cognitive impairment, avoid anticholinergics, benzodiazepines, Z-drugs, and chronic antipsychotics because of adverse CNS effects. Cumulative anticholinergic exposure is associated with falls, delirium, and dementia.

title: A shunt helps normal-pressure hydrocephalus when gait leads
lead: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus is considered for a shunt when gait is the leading problem and a tap improves it. A cortical dementia is not shunted.
lines: The order of symptoms matters: gait, then bladder, then mind.
Large ventricles with little cortical atrophy are the scan.
A patient whose memory failed first is not this disease.
Gait, then bladder, then cognition. Ventricles large, cortex relatively spared, opening pressure not high.
A tap that improves gait is the patient considered for a shunt. Memory-first disease is not shunted.
miss: Shunting a patient with years of isolated memory loss.

source.name: AAN practice guideline update summary: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus.
source.says: Shunting is possibly effective in iNPH. Clinicians may counsel patients that a positive response to external lumbar drainage or to repeated lumbar punctures increases the chance of response to shunting (Level C).

title: A large brain abscess is drained
lead: A brain abscess that is large or not responding is drained. Antibiotics alone are for a small abscess in a patient you can follow.
lines: The source, ear, sinus, or heart, is treated too.
Steroids are for significant edema, not for every ring.
A lumbar puncture is not how you make this diagnosis.
Image before the lumbar puncture when a focal sign or papilledema is present.
miss: Six weeks of antibiotics and no drainage for a 4-centimeter lesion with a worsening exam.

source.name: ESCMID guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of brain abscess in children and adults.
source.says: MRI is recommended for diagnosis. Aspiration or excision of brain abscess is recommended whenever feasible, except for toxoplasmosis. Adjunctive glucocorticoids are recommended for severe symptoms from perifocal oedema or impending herniation.

title: Horner syndrome gets a carotid and an apex
lead: A painful Horner syndrome is a carotid dissection until imaged. A painless one in a smoker includes the lung apex.
lines: The pupil is small. Do not start pilocarpine thinking it is a dilated pupil.
A brainstem stroke can cause it with other signs. Those signs decide the scanner.
An isolated chronic Horner still gets an explanation.
Ptosis and miosis from lost sympathetics. A third-nerve palsy is a down-and-out eye with a blown pupil.
miss: Calling a painful small pupil a migraine and sending the patient home.

source.name: ACR Appropriateness Criteria. Horner Syndrome.
source.says: For acute painful Horner syndrome, and for nonacute nonlocalizable Horner syndrome, CTA head and neck with IV contrast is rated usually appropriate as initial imaging.

title: A TIA is a stroke warning, not a cleared patient
lead: A transient ischemic attack is treated as a threatened stroke. Antiplatelet therapy, a cause, and a same-day or next-day plan are the visit.
lines: Atrial fibrillation found on the tracing changes the drug to anticoagulation.
A high-grade carotid stenosis is a surgical conversation.
The symptoms resolving does not mean the risk resolved.
miss: Reassuring a patient whose hand weakness resolved and scheduling clinic in a month.
diagramAlt: TIA before discharge. Antithrombotic today AF found: anticoagulant, not aspirin Carotid imaging, not a visit in 3 months

source.name: 2021 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack.
source.says: Diagnostic tests for the cause of a TIA should be completed within 48 hours when possible. Prescribe antithrombotic therapy; screen for atrial fibrillation and anticoagulate if found; consider endarterectomy or stenting for severe ipsilateral carotid stenosis.

title: Cord compression gets steroids and a surgeon or radiation
lead: Spinal cord compression is dexamethasone and urgent decompression or radiation. Plain films are not the test.
lines: Back pain plus a sensory level, bilateral weakness, or new bladder failure is the syndrome.
MRI is the image.
Cancer is the common cause in an adult. Treat the cord before the staging is complete.
Bilateral weakness, a sensory level, or new retention is the syndrome. Decompress. Do not wait for full cancer staging.
miss: Ordering outpatient lumbar films for a patient who cannot urinate.
diagramAlt: Cord compression. Dexamethasone immediately MRI today, not plain films Decompress. Do not wait for full staging

source.name: NICE NG234. Spinal metastases and metastatic spinal cord compression.
source.says: Offer MRI to people with suspected MSCC and do not use plain X-ray of the spine to diagnose or rule it out. Offer 16 mg of oral dexamethasone as soon as possible and continue it daily while awaiting surgery or radiotherapy.

title: Do not image ordinary back pain
lead: Acute low back pain without a red flag does not get imaging in the first six weeks.
lines: Red flags that change the plan: cancer history, unexplained weight loss, fever, injection-drug use, recent spinal infection or bacteremia, trauma, progressive deficit, saddle anesthesia, or new bowel or bladder loss.
Cauda equina is an MRI and a surgical call, not a course of ibuprofen.
Early imaging without a flag finds incidental disease and does not speed recovery.
miss: Ordering an MRI for two days of mechanical pain because the patient asked for one.
diagramAlt: Image the back now. Cauda equina, cancer, infection, deficit Otherwise no MRI in the first weeks Activity, not bed rest

source.name: ACR Appropriateness Criteria. Low Back Pain: 2021 Update.
source.says: Uncomplicated acute low back pain with or without radiculopathy does not warrant imaging. Imaging is considered after up to 6 weeks of medical management with little or no improvement, or with red flags such as cauda equina syndrome, malignancy, fracture, or infection.

more.name: ACP high-value care advice: diagnostic imaging for low back pain (2011)

title: Treat the gout flare
lead: A gout flare is treated with colchicine, an NSAID, or a glucocorticoid. Allopurinol alone is not the treatment of the flare.
lines: Anti-inflammatory therapy treats the flare. Urate-lowering therapy is the long plan and is not a substitute for treating the flare.
Colchicine works best within about 36 hours of onset. Lower the dose when the GFR is reduced.
If urate-lowering therapy is already prescribed, continue it through the flare. Do not start it alone as the pain plan.
Choose the anti-inflammatory the kidneys and the stomach allow. An opioid does not treat the crystal inflammation.
miss: Starting allopurinol during a hot joint and sending the patient home on that alone.
diagramAlt: Gout flare drug. Colchicine, NSAID, or glucocorticoid Not allopurinol as the only drug Continue allopurinol if already taking it

source.name: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout.
source.says: For a gout flare, oral colchicine, NSAIDs, or glucocorticoids (oral, intraarticular, or intramuscular) are strongly recommended as first-line therapy, chosen by patient factors. Patients already taking urate-lowering therapy should continue it.

title: Fasciotomy is the treatment of a tight compartment
lead: Acute compartment syndrome is opened. Analgesia and elevation do not replace the fasciotomy.
lines: Pain on passive stretch is enough to call the surgeon. A pulse can still be present.
Remove the cast or the dressing first if that is the cause, and reassess immediately.
The limb is not observed overnight once the diagnosis is made.
Pulselessness is late. Remove the cast and call for fasciotomy. More opioid is not the treatment.
miss: Increasing the opioid and rechecking the compartment in the morning.
diagramAlt: Compartment, do not wait for the pulse. Pain out of proportion Pain on passive stretch Fasciotomy. Pulse loss is late

source.name: AAOS Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Acute Compartment Syndrome (case-based summary).
source.says: Serial clinical examinations can assist in ruling in acute compartment syndrome; compartment pressure monitoring can assist but is not always necessary. A diastolic-to-compartment pressure difference of 30 mm Hg can be used as a threshold for diagnosis and fasciotomy.

title: Inflammatory back pain is treated with an NSAID and movement
lead: Ankylosing spondylitis is treated with an NSAID and with activity. Rest is the wrong prescription.
lines: A TNF inhibitor is the next step when NSAIDs fail and the diagnosis is secure.
Uveitis is treated as uveitis, urgently, not with the same oral NSAID plan alone.
A young man whose pain is worse in the morning is not given six weeks of bed rest.
An NSAID is first-line. A red painful eye is acute anterior uveitis and is same-day ophthalmology.
miss: Prescribing bed rest for morning stiffness that improves with walking.

source.name: 2019 ACR/SAA/SPARTAN Recommendations for the Treatment of Ankylosing Spondylitis and Nonradiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis.
source.says: NSAIDs are strongly recommended over no NSAIDs, and physical therapy over no physical therapy. In active AS despite NSAIDs, a TNF inhibitor is strongly recommended over no TNF inhibitor.

title: Adult dermatomyositis gets a cancer search
lead: Adult dermatomyositis is treated with immunosuppression and is searched for cancer. The rash is not sent to dermatology alone.
lines: Proximal weakness is the function you measure.
Interstitial lung disease is asked about and imaged when the story fits.
A statin myopathy has no Gottron papules. Stop the statin, but do not miss the rash.
Adults get a cancer search. Immunosuppression treats the muscle. A statin myopathy has no rash.
miss: Prescribing a topical steroid for Gottron papules and ignoring the shoulders.

source.name: International Guideline for Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy-Associated Cancer Screening (IMACS).
source.says: Dermatomyositis carries the highest cancer risk among myositis subtypes. All adults with new-onset myositis should be tested for myositis-specific and myositis-associated autoantibodies to stratify cancer risk, which then sets screening modality and frequency.

title: Psoriatic arthritis is treated as a joint disease
lead: Psoriatic arthritis is treated even when the skin is mild. A TNF inhibitor or another targeted drug is used when NSAIDs are not enough.
lines: Dactylitis and DIP disease are the clues on the exam.
Nail pitting counts. Ask the patient to show the scalp.
Methotrexate is a common conventional drug. It is not the only option when the joints are eroding.
DIP joints, nail pits, and a whole-digit dactylitis. Rheumatoid arthritis prefers MCP and PIP joints and spares the DIP.
miss: Treating only the skin plaques while the digit stays swollen.

source.name: 2018 ACR/NPF Guideline for the Treatment of Psoriatic Arthritis.
source.says: In treatment-naive active psoriatic arthritis, a TNF inhibitor biologic is conditionally recommended over an oral small molecule such as methotrexate as a first-line option; methotrexate is recommended over NSAIDs.

title: Reactive arthritis: treat the germ if it is still there
lead: A persistent triggering infection is treated. The sterile joint itself is treated with an NSAID, not with weeks of unnecessary broad antibiotics.
lines: A tap that is culture-negative is the point.
Uveitis needs an eye exam.
A single dose of antibiotics does not fix established joint inflammation.
Sterile inflammatory joint days to weeks after Chlamydia or a gut infection. Culture of the fluid is negative.
miss: Operating a culture-negative knee or giving a month of vancomycin.

source.name: StatPearls. Reactive Arthritis.
source.says: NSAIDs are first-line therapy for acute reactive arthritis. Antibiotics are not recommended for the arthritis itself but may be indicated for the primary infection, especially Chlamydia trachomatis.

title: Marfan syndrome is followed at the aortic root
lead: Marfan syndrome dilates the aortic root and can dislocate the lens. The long fingers are not what shortens life.
lines: Reported incidence is about 1 in 3000 to 5000, and inheritance is autosomal dominant.
Aortic regurgitation and aneurysm are the cardiovascular findings.
There is no diagnostic blood test other than testing the gene.
miss: Calling the syndrome benign because the patient is tall and has no chest pain.
diagramAlt: Marfan syndrome. FBN1 makes fibrillin Aortic root dilatation is the danger Lens dislocation is the eye finding

source.name: StatPearls. Marfan Syndrome.
source.says: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder with a reported incidence of 1 in 3000 to 5000 individuals.

more.name: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease

title: Pemphigus is a steroid disease and the mouth is involved
lead: Moderate-to-severe pemphigus has an intravenous CD20 inhibitor as a first-line option. The mouth is involved, and the blisters are flaccid.
lines: Nikolsky-positive flaccid bullae are the exam.
Fluid and wound care matter because the skin barrier is gone.
Bullous pemphigoid is tense and is a different, usually less mucosal, disease.
Systemic corticosteroid plus a steroid-sparing drug. Topical therapy alone does not treat widespread disease.
miss: Prescribing nystatin alone for months of oral erosions and skin loss.

source.name: International consensus on pemphigus management (Joly et al.).
source.says: This international consensus includes intravenous CD20 inhibitors (rituximab, ofatumumab) as a first-line therapy option for moderate-to-severe pemphigus, alongside systemic corticosteroids.

title: A septic native joint is washed and covered for staph
lead: After the tap, a septic native joint is washed and treated with antibiotics that cover Staphylococcus aureus until the culture narrows them.
lines: Gonorrhea is the exception to think of in a young sexually active patient, and the culture includes it.
A prosthetic joint is a different operation and a different biofilm regimen.
Oral step-down happens after the source is controlled, not on day one of a toxic patient.
Tap before antibiotics if the patient is stable. Staphylococcus aureus is the native-joint organism to cover.
miss: Leaving a purulent knee on intravenous antibiotics without drainage.

source.name: StatPearls. Septic Arthritis.
source.says: Staphylococcus aureus is the most common organism in adults. Arthrocentesis should be done without delay; treatment is antimicrobial therapy with antistaphylococcal coverage plus joint drainage by aspiration, arthroscopy, or arthrotomy.

more.name: PIDS/IDSA guideline for acute bacterial arthritis in children (2023)

title: Hip fracture is operated early and protected from clot
lead: A hip fracture in an older adult is operated as soon as the patient is medically ready, generally within a day or two, and is given clot prophylaxis.
lines: Pain is treated so the patient can move. Delirium is prevented by that, by glasses, and by not adding anticholinergics.
A fragility fracture means treat the osteoporosis. Do not wait for an outpatient DEXA to name the disease.
Urinary catheters come out.
miss: Waiting a week for the internist to clear a stable patient.
diagramAlt: Hip fracture timing. Operate within about 48 hours if ready Prophylax against clot A fragility fracture starts osteoporosis treatment

source.name: NICE CG124. Hip fracture: management.
source.says: Perform surgery on the day of, or the day after, admission. Care should also follow NICE guidance on venous thromboembolism, delirium, and osteoporosis fragility-fracture risk assessment.

more.name: AAOS Management of Hip Fractures in Older Adults CPG (2021)

title: Osteogenesis imperfecta does not cancel a child-protection question
lead: Fractures from osteogenesis imperfecta are real, and inflicted injury is still considered. Blue sclerae do not end the duty to protect a child.
lines: The pattern of the fracture, the history, and the developmental stage are the questions.
Both diagnoses can be true.
Hearing and dental findings support the collagen disease and are documented.
Type I collagen. Blue sclerae, fractures with little force, and hearing loss.
Blue sclerae do not close a child-protection question. Inflicted injury and this disease can both be present.
miss: Closing a child-protection evaluation because the sclerae are blue.

source.name: AAP Clinical Report. Evaluating Children With Fractures for Child Physical Abuse.
source.says: Fractures are common injuries caused by child abuse. The report reviews fracture specificity, mechanism, and medical diseases that predispose to fractures, to guide an evidence-based differential diagnosis and evaluation of a child with fractures.

title: Necrotizing infection goes to the operating room
lead: Necrotizing fasciitis is taken to surgery when it is suspected. Broad antibiotics start on the way. Imaging that delays the room is the miss.
lines: Necrotizing fasciitis is a life-threatening skin and soft tissue infection in the 2014 IDSA guideline.
The recommendation is prompt diagnosis and timely effective treatment, not a day of antibiotics to see if the skin improves.
Pain beyond the visible skin, toxicity, and a rising lactate are the clinical clues. Crepitus is not required.
Pain beyond the skin you can see, with toxicity, goes to the operating room the same day. Antibiotics alone are not the plan.
miss: Observing suspected necrotizing fasciitis overnight on antibiotics alone.

source.name: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Skin and Soft Tissue Infections: 2014 Update.
source.says: Prompt surgical consultation is recommended for aggressive infections with systemic toxicity or suspected necrotizing fasciitis or gas gangrene (strong). Empiric antibiotics should be broad, e.g., vancomycin or linezolid plus piperacillin-tazobactam or a carbapenem.

title: The ACS clocks
lead: A 12-lead ECG is due within 10 minutes of first medical contact. A STEMI does not wait for the troponin.
lines: STEMI goes to a PCI-capable hospital. The system goal is first medical contact to device in 90 minutes.
If the patient arrives at a hospital that cannot do PCI, the transfer goal is 120 minutes. If that will be missed, give fibrinolysis.
A nondiagnostic first ECG with ongoing pain gets serial ECGs, including posterior leads when the story fits.
Acquire and interpret a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes. Primary PCI targets are 90 minutes at a PCI-capable hospital and 120 minutes when transfer is required.
miss: Waiting for a troponin before activating the lab for ST elevation.
diagramAlt: ACS time goals. ECG within 10 minutes of contact PCI hospital: device by 90 minutes Transfer: 120 minutes, or give a lytic

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: In suspected ACS, a 12-lead ECG should be acquired and interpreted within 10 minutes of first medical contact. Suspected STEMI goes to a PCI-capable hospital with an FMC-to-first-device goal of 90 minutes or less; direct transport may be considered if the anticipated FMC-to-device time is 120 minutes or less.

more.name: Medscape guideline summary of the 2025 ACC/AHA ACS guideline

title: The four pillars, and the improved EF
lead: HFrEF gets all four: an ARNI, an evidence-based beta blocker, a mineralocorticoid antagonist, and an SGLT2 inhibitor.
lines: The evidence-based beta blockers are carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol.
If the EF later rises above 40%, this is improved EF. Keep the HFrEF drugs.
A small rise in creatinine after the start is expected. It is not, by itself, a reason to stop the drug that keeps the patient alive.
The four drugs are an ARNI (or ACE inhibitor or ARB if an ARNI cannot be used), carvedilol or metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol, an MRA, and an SGLT2 inhibitor.
miss: Stopping the ACE inhibitor or the ARNI because the creatinine rose from 1.1 to 1.3, and never restarting it.
diagramAlt: Four pillars for HFrEF: ARNI, evidence-based beta blocker, mineralocorticoid antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor. Improved ejection fraction stays on this therapy.

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: GDMT for HFrEF now includes 4 medication classes: renin-angiotensin system inhibition with ARNi, ACEi, or ARB; beta blockers; MRAs; and SGLT2i. Beta blockers with proven benefit are bisoprolol, carvedilol, and sustained-release metoprolol succinate.

title: Who with atrial fibrillation gets an anticoagulant
lead: Anticoagulate when the yearly stroke risk is about 2% or higher. For CHA2DS2-VASc, that is 2 or more in men and 3 or more in women.
lines: Use a DOAC rather than warfarin unless there is moderate or severe mitral stenosis or a mechanical valve.
The pattern of the fibrillation, paroxysmal or permanent, does not change the indication.
Aspirin is not stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation.
Class 1 anticoagulation starts at an estimated yearly risk of at least 2%. DOACs are preferred except for moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis and mechanical valves.
miss: Prescribing aspirin because the CHA2DS2-VASc score felt too low for a DOAC, or withholding a DOAC because the patient is often in sinus rhythm.
diagramAlt: Who gets anticoagulation. Class 1: ≥2% per year Men CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2, women ≥3 DOAC, except mitral stenosis or metal valve

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: For AF with an estimated annual thromboembolic risk of 2% or more per year (eg, CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or more in men, 3 or more in women), anticoagulation is recommended. DOACs are recommended over warfarin except with moderate to severe rheumatic mitral stenosis or a mechanical heart valve; aspirin is not an alternative.

title: Stage 2 hypertension starts two drugs
lead: In the 2025 blood-pressure guideline, a pressure of 140/90 or higher starts two agents from different classes, preferably in one pill.
lines: The treatment goal for most adults is under 130/80, and a higher-risk patient is encouraged toward a systolic pressure under 120.
Risk is estimated with PREVENT, not the old pooled cohort equation.
Stage 1 with cardiovascular disease, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, or a 10-year risk of at least 7.5% starts a drug. Lower risk gets 3 to 6 months of lifestyle first.
Stage 2 hypertension is treated with two agents. The goal is under 130/80, using the PREVENT equations for risk.
miss: Starting one drug at 162/98 and rechecking in six months.
diagramAlt: 2025 blood-pressure start. ≥140/90: two drugs, one pill if possible Goal under 130/80 for most adults Stage 1: drug now if PREVENT ≥7.5%

source.name: 2025 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults.
source.says: Stage 2 hypertension (140/90 or higher) starts drug therapy with 2 first-line agents of different classes, preferably as a single-pill combination. The goal is under 130/80 for all adults. Stage 1 starts a drug with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT 10-year risk of 7.5% or more; otherwise after a 3- to 6-month lifestyle trial.

title: Do not give thrombolysis for a STEMI you can open
lead: A STEMI that can reach a PCI-capable lab within the time goal goes to PCI, not to fibrinolysis.
lines: First medical contact to device is 90 minutes at a PCI hospital and 120 minutes if transfer is required.
If that transfer will miss 120 minutes, give a fibrinolytic and do not keep waiting.
A posterior lead and a repeat ECG catch the STEMI the first tracing missed.
ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact. Do not wait for troponin to activate the lab for ST elevation.
miss: Giving a fibrinolytic in the parking lot of a PCI hospital.
diagramAlt: ACS time goals. ECG within 10 minutes of contact PCI hospital: device by 90 minutes Transfer: 120 minutes, or give a lytic

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: For STEMI within 12 hours, primary PCI with an FMC-to-device target of 90 minutes or less at a PCI-capable hospital, or 120 minutes or less when transfer is required. Give fibrinolytic therapy if expected delay to primary PCI is more than 2 hours from FMC and there are no contraindications.

title: Oxygen in ACS is for hypoxia, not for the diagnosis
lead: A patient with suspected ACS and a normal oxygen saturation does not get routine oxygen.
lines: Give oxygen when the saturation is low or the patient is in distress from hypoxia.
Aspirin, if there is no allergy or active bleeding, is the drug that is actually indicated.
A STEMI still does not wait for the troponin.
Routine oxygen is not recommended when saturation is normal. Reperfusion and aspirin are the time-critical actions.
A nondiagnostic ECG with ongoing pain gets a repeat tracing, including posterior leads when the story fits.
miss: Putting every chest-pain patient on a nonrebreather.

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: In ACS with oxygen saturation 90% or higher, routine supplemental oxygen is not recommended because it does not improve outcomes. With confirmed hypoxia (saturation under 90%), supplemental oxygen to raise saturation to 90% or more is recommended.

title: Improved ejection fraction stays on the four drugs
lead: If the ejection fraction was 40% or lower and later rises, keep the HFrEF drugs. This is improved ejection fraction, not a cure.
lines: Stopping the ARNI or the beta blocker because the number looks better is how patients bounce back.
A small creatinine rise after the start is expected.
The evidence-based beta blockers remain carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol.
The four drugs are an ARNI (or ACE inhibitor or ARB if an ARNI cannot be used), carvedilol or metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol, an MRA, and an SGLT2 inhibitor.
miss: Declaring the heart failure gone because the ejection fraction is now 45%.
diagramAlt: Start before discharge. ARNI, evidence-based beta blocker MRA and SGLT2 inhibitor Clinic within 7 days

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: Patients with HFrEF whose LVEF improves to above 40% have HFimpEF and should continue HFrEF treatment; GDMT should be continued to prevent relapse of HF and LV dysfunction, even if asymptomatic.

title: Cardioversion does not cancel the anticoagulant
lead: Restoring sinus rhythm does not remove the stroke risk that required anticoagulation.
lines: The indication is the yearly risk, not the rhythm on today's ECG.
Aspirin is not the substitute.
Class 1 anticoagulation is an estimated risk of at least 2% per year: CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 or more in men and 3 or more in women.
A DOAC is preferred. Exceptions are moderate or severe mitral stenosis and a mechanical valve, which stay on warfarin. Aspirin does not prevent stroke. Sinus rhythm does not cancel the indication.
miss: Stopping the DOAC the week after a successful cardioversion.
diagramAlt: Who gets anticoagulation. Class 1: ≥2% per year Men CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2, women ≥3 DOAC, except mitral stenosis or metal valve

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: Anticoagulation is recommended for AF with an estimated annual thromboembolic risk of 2% or more (eg, CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or more in men, 3 or more in women). Continued anticoagulation is recommended early after conversion to sinus rhythm; aspirin is not an alternative to anticoagulation.

title: A mechanical valve or mitral stenosis still gets warfarin
lead: A DOAC is not the anticoagulant for moderate or severe mitral stenosis or for a mechanical valve. Those patients get warfarin.
lines: The rest of nonvalvular atrial fibrillation prefers a DOAC.
A bioprosthetic valve is not the same instruction as a mechanical valve.
The INR target follows the valve, not a guess of 2 to 3 for every prosthesis.
Warfarin is the anticoagulant. A DOAC is not substituted at discharge.
Write the INR target for that valve. Aspirin may be added for some prostheses and does not replace warfarin.
miss: Switching a mechanical mitral valve to apixaban because the patient dislikes blood tests.
diagramAlt: Who still needs warfarin. Mechanical valve Moderate or severe mitral stenosis A DOAC is otherwise preferred in AF

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: In AF with rheumatic mitral stenosis or mitral stenosis of moderate or greater severity, long-term warfarin is recommended over DOACs. Warfarin remains first-line therapy with a mechanical heart valve. In other valve disease, DOACs are recommended over VKAs.

title: Endocarditis antibiotics wait for cultures if the patient can wait
lead: In a stable patient with suspected endocarditis, draw the blood cultures before the antibiotic.
lines: Three sets from separate sticks are the usual ask.
An unstable patient gets the drug after whatever cultures you can draw immediately.
A dental procedure prophylaxis is for a short list of heart lesions, not for every murmur.
Acute on a normal valve is Staphylococcus aureus. Subacute on an abnormal valve is viridans streptococci.
Three culture sets from separate sites before antibiotics if the patient is stable. Prophylaxis is only for the highest-risk hearts, not for an isolated click.
miss: Giving one dose of an oral antibiotic and then trying to culture the blood the next day.
diagramAlt: Endocarditis cultures. Three sets, separate sticks Before antibiotics if the patient can wait Prophylaxis only for the highest-risk hearts

source.name: StatPearls. Infective Endocarditis.
source.says: Diagnosis uses blood cultures and echocardiography. AHA and ACC guidance limits antibiotic prophylaxis to patients at highest risk of adverse outcomes from endocarditis who undergo dental procedures that manipulate gingival or periapical tissue or perforate the oral mucosa.

title: Type A dissection is an operation
lead: A dissection that involves the ascending aorta goes to surgery. Blood pressure is lowered with a beta blocker first so the shear falls.
lines: A pure vasodilator first can raise the force of contraction. The beta blocker comes before or with it.
Unequal pulses are the bedside clue you already have.
Thrombolysis is contraindicated.
Unequal arm pressures or pulses and tearing pain to the back. Give a beta blocker before a pure vasodilator.
Involvement of the ascending aorta is an operation. A fibrinolytic extends the tear.
miss: Starting nicardipine alone, or giving a fibrinolytic for the chest pain.
diagramAlt: Ascending dissection. Beta blocker before a pure vasodilator Type A: operating room No fibrinolytic

source.name: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease.
source.says: Suspected or confirmed acute type A aortic dissection warrants emergency surgical consultation and immediate surgical intervention. Initial management of acute aortic syndrome includes intravenous beta blockers, adding intravenous vasodilators if BP is not controlled after beta-blocker therapy.

title: A rupturing aneurysm does not go to the clinic
lead: Hypotension, back or abdominal pain, and a known or pulsatile aneurysm is rupture. The patient goes to repair, not to a repeat ultrasound.
lines: Permissive hypotension until the aorta is controlled. A large crystalloid bolus before control can worsen bleeding.
Do not repeatedly palpate a tender aneurysm.
A stable incidental aneurysm is a diameter and a risk discussion. Smoking cessation slows growth. It is not tonight's emergency.
miss: Sending the hypotensive patient for a clinic ultrasound this week.

source.name: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease.
source.says: In ruptured AAA, permissive hypotension can be beneficial to decrease the rate of bleeding; rupture protocols aim at immediate transfer to the operating room for prompt hemorrhage control and repair.

more.name: SVS practice guidelines on the care of patients with an abdominal aortic aneurysm (2018)

title: Tamponade is drained, not diuresed
lead: Tamponade is treated by removing the pericardial fluid. A diuretic reduces the preload the heart still needed.
lines: Fluids are a bridge while the needle or the window is arranged.
A small effusion without equalization is not tamponade and does not need an emergency window.
Diastolic pressures equalize and the y descent drops. Pulsus paradoxus is an exaggerated inspiratory fall in systolic pressure.
Fluids are a bridge. Drainage is the treatment. A diuretic removes the last preload.
miss: Giving furosemide for the distended neck veins.

source.name: 2015 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases.
source.says: Treatment of cardiac tamponade is drainage of the pericardial fluid, preferably by needle pericardiocentesis with echocardiographic or fluoroscopic guidance, performed without delay in unstable patients (class I).

title: Torsades gets magnesium, and the QT drug stops
lead: Torsades de pointes is treated with intravenous magnesium and by stopping the QT-prolonging drug. A stable patient is not given another QT-prolonging antiarrhythmic.
lines: Correct potassium.
Unstable polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is defibrillated.
A congenital long QT with syncope is a specialist and often a defibrillator conversation, not a higher dose of the offending antibiotic.
Stop the QT-prolonging drug. Do not give amiodarone or another QT-prolonging antiarrhythmic for torsades.
miss: Giving amiodarone for polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in a patient whose QT is already long.

source.name: StatPearls. Torsade de Pointes.
source.says: Intravenous magnesium is the first-line pharmacologic therapy in torsades de pointes; magnesium is thought to stabilize the cardiac membrane.

title: Typical flutter can be ablated at the isthmus
lead: Typical atrial flutter is treated by ablating the cavotricuspid isthmus when the patient is a candidate. Rate and stroke prevention still matter today.
lines: A ventricular rate of 150 with sawtooth waves is flutter until proved otherwise.
Adenosine may show the flutter waves. It does not cure the circuit.
Anticoagulate at an estimated yearly stroke risk of at least 2% (CHA2DS2-VASc at least 2 in men or 3 in women). Use a DOAC unless there is moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis or a mechanical valve.
Ablation of the isthmus treats the circuit. Stroke prevention follows the same risk threshold as fibrillation and is not cancelled by sinus rhythm.
miss: Cardioverting and stopping anticoagulation because the ECG is now sinus.

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: Anticoagulation is recommended for an estimated annual thromboembolic risk of 2% or more (eg, CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or more in men, 3 or more in women), with DOACs over warfarin except moderate to severe rheumatic mitral stenosis or a mechanical valve. Patients after flutter ablation are not free from thromboembolic risk.

more.name: StatPearls. Atrial Flutter.

title: HFpEF still gets an SGLT2 inhibitor conversation
lead: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is treated for congestion and for the comorbidities. An SGLT2 inhibitor is the drug class with a recommendation, not a loop diuretic alone forever.
lines: The 2022 guideline gives SGLT2 inhibitors a class 2a recommendation in HFpEF.
Blood pressure control is part of the disease, using the current hypertension goal.
Do not apply the four-pillar HFrEF list unchanged and add a beta blocker that the patient does not otherwise need.
miss: Stopping all heart-failure drugs because the ejection fraction is 60% while the patient is still admitted for congestion.

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: New recommendations for HF with preserved EF are made for SGLT2i (COR 2a), MRAs (COR 2b), and ARNi (COR 2b). In HFpEF, SGLT2i can be beneficial in decreasing HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality.

title: Rheumatic fever prevention is penicillin, not a one-time antibiotic
lead: After rheumatic fever, secondary prevention is scheduled penicillin. Treating one sore throat does not finish the job.
lines: The duration depends on whether the heart was involved and on how long ago the attack was.
A new pharyngitis is still treated. Prevention is in addition.
The mitral valve is what you listen to for the rest of the patient's life.
Mitral valve is the most affected. Jones criteria diagnose acute rheumatic fever. The chronic valve lesion is years later.
miss: Giving a single course of amoxicillin and discharging the prevention plan.
diagramAlt: Rheumatic prophylaxis. After rheumatic fever: scheduled penicillin Duration depends on carditis One 10-day course is not prophylaxis

source.name: AHA Scientific Statement. Prevention of rheumatic fever and diagnosis and treatment of acute streptococcal pharyngitis.
