source.says: A person who has had rheumatic fever is at very high risk of recurrence after GAS pharyngitis and needs continuous antimicrobial prophylaxis (secondary prevention). Duration depends on number of attacks, time since the last attack, exposure risk, age, and cardiac involvement.

title: A tet spell is calmed, and the resistance is raised
lead: A hypercyanotic spell in tetralogy is treated by calming the child, giving oxygen, and raising systemic resistance, including knees-to-chest.
lines: A vasoconstrictor is the drug version of squatting when the spell continues.
A drug that drops afterload makes the right-to-left shunt worse.
The murmur getting softer means less blood is crossing the pulmonary valve.
Pulmonic stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy, overriding aorta, VSD. A spell is infundibular spasm.
Knees-to-chest raises systemic resistance and sends blood to the lungs. A vasodilator does the opposite. The murmur gets softer as less blood crosses the valve.
miss: Giving a pure vasodilator during a spell.
diagramAlt: Hypercyanotic spell. Knees to chest. Oxygen. Calm Raise systemic resistance A vasodilator worsens the right-to-left shunt

source.name: StatPearls. Tetralogy of Fallot.
source.says: Tet spells need knee-chest positioning to increase systemic vascular resistance, oxygen, and sometimes intravenous beta-blockers or intravenous phenylephrine to increase systemic afterload. Morphine can be given as a sedative.

title: GOLD group E is one exacerbation
lead: In GOLD 2026, one moderate or severe exacerbation in the past year is group E. Start a LABA plus a LAMA, not a LABA plus an inhaled steroid alone.
lines: Group A has no such exacerbation and few symptoms: a bronchodilator.
One moderate or severe exacerbation now places a treatment-naive patient in group E. Initial therapy for group E is LABA/LAMA, with triple therapy considered at eosinophils of at least 300.
Add the inhaled steroid as triple therapy when blood eosinophils are at least 300 cells per microliter. Do not start an ICS/LABA pair for COPD without asthma.
miss: Using the old rule that one exacerbation was not enough to leave group A, and starting an ICS/LABA.
diagramAlt: GOLD 2026 groups. No exacerbation and few symptoms: bronchodilator. No exacerbation and more symptoms: LABA plus LAMA. One or more moderate or severe exacerbations: LABA plus LAMA, and consider triple therapy if eosinophils are at least 300.

source.name: GOLD 2027 Report. Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD.
source.says: Group E now includes one moderate exacerbation in the previous year. LABA+LAMA is the preferred initial therapy in group E; consider LABA+LAMA+ICS as initial therapy if blood eosinophils are 300 cells/µL or more. Use of LABA+ICS in COPD is not encouraged.

title: No SABA-only asthma plan
lead: Every adolescent and adult with asthma gets an inhaled corticosteroid. As-needed albuterol alone is not a plan.
lines: GINA track 1 uses ICS-formoterol as the reliever at every step.
Steps 1 and 2 are as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol. From step 3 it is also the daily maintenance inhaler.
A short course of systemic steroid treats a severe flare. It is not controller therapy.
GINA recommends against SABA-only treatment. ICS-formoterol is the preferred anti-inflammatory reliever and reduces severe exacerbations compared with SABA-based care.
In an acute attack, oxygen only if saturation is under 92%, and the target is at or under 95% for adults and adolescents.
miss: Refilling albuterol for daily symptoms and calling the asthma mild.
diagramAlt: Acute asthma oxygen. No oxygen if saturation ≥92% If given, target ≤95% in adults Preferred reliever: ICS-formoterol

source.name: GINA 2026 Summary Guide for Asthma Management and Prevention.
source.says: Adults, adolescents and children 6-11 years with asthma should not be treated with SABA alone; all should receive ICS-containing treatment. Steps 1-2: as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol. Steps 3-5: ICS-formoterol as daily maintenance plus as-needed doses (MART).

title: Where to treat community pneumonia
lead: The first pneumonia decision is the site of care, using severity, not a single lab. Anaerobic coverage is not routine for aspiration.
lines: Healthy outpatients: amoxicillin or doxycycline. A macrolide only where pneumococcal resistance is under 25%.
Comorbid outpatients: a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or doxycycline, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone.
Site of care is based on severity. Regimens are split by comorbidity and by ward versus ICU. Routine anaerobic coverage for suspected aspiration is not recommended.
miss: Adding metronidazole because the word aspiration appeared, or admitting a low-risk patient for an IV drug that an oral regimen covers.
diagramAlt: Pneumonia: where and which drug. Hypoxia, shock, or confusion: admit Severe: beta-lactam + macrolide No routine anaerobic drug for aspiration

source.name: 2019 ATS/IDSA Guideline for Diagnosis and Treatment of Adults with Community-acquired Pneumonia.
source.says: Healthy outpatients: amoxicillin 1 g every 8 hours or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily; a macrolide only where pneumococcal macrolide resistance is under 25%. Use the PSI with clinical judgment for site of care. Do not routinely add anaerobic coverage for suspected aspiration unless lung abscess or empyema is suspected.

title: Who with a pulmonary embolus gets a lytic
lead: Systemic thrombolysis is for high-risk pulmonary embolism with hypotension or shock. A stable patient is anticoagulated and risk-stratified.
lines: Start anticoagulation when the probability is high and bleeding risk is not prohibitive, even before the confirmatory scan, if the scan will be delayed.
A DOAC is appropriate for most stable patients. Thrombolysis is not.
Right-heart strain with a normal blood pressure is intermediate risk. It is not an automatic lytic.
Systolic pressure under 90 mm Hg or shock is high-risk and gets reperfusion. A normal pressure gets anticoagulation.
miss: Giving a lytic because the CT said massive clot, while the blood pressure is normal.
diagramAlt: Pulmonary embolism split. Hypotension or shock: reperfuse Normal pressure: anticoagulate Right-heart strain alone is not a lytic

source.name: 2026 AHA/ACC/Multisociety Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism in Adults (Guideline-at-a-Glance).
source.says: Systemic thrombolysis plus anticoagulation is reasonable in PE with persistent hypotension or cardiogenic shock (Category E) and acceptable bleeding risk. In categories A1-C2 it should not be used over anticoagulation alone (harm). DOACs are recommended over VKAs for eligible patients.

more.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism

title: Do not stop the SGLT2 inhibitor for the early dip
lead: Start an SGLT2 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes and CKD when eGFR is at least 20, and for CKD with heart failure or with albuminuria at least 200 mg/g.
lines: The early eGFR dip is hemodynamic. It is not a reason to stop.
Continue the drug if eGFR later falls below 20, unless it is not tolerated or dialysis starts.
Hold it for prolonged fasting, surgery, or critical illness, because of ketosis.
miss: Stopping the drug at the two-week lab because eGFR fell from 48 to 42.

source.name: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease.
source.says: Treat T2D with CKD and eGFR 20 or more with an SGLT2i (1A), and adults with CKD and eGFR 20 or more with ACR 200 mg/g or more, or heart failure (1A). Continue if eGFR falls below 20 unless not tolerated or KRT starts. The reversible eGFR decrease on initiation is generally not a reason to stop.

title: Group A COPD is a bronchodilator, not an inhaled steroid
lead: GOLD 2026 group A, no exacerbation and few symptoms, starts a bronchodilator. An inhaled steroid is not the opening drug.
lines: Initial therapy is a bronchodilator for group A and dual long-acting bronchodilation for groups B and E.
Group B (symptoms, no exacerbation) and group E (one moderate or severe exacerbation) start LABA plus LAMA, not LABA/ICS.
Consider triple therapy when blood eosinophils are at least 300/µL. That is not the default starting inhaler.
A flare is a separate decision: a systemic steroid for about 5 days, and an antibiotic only if sputum turns purulent plus more dyspnea or volume.
miss: Starting every smoker on an ICS/LABA inhaler.
diagramAlt: GOLD 2026, who gets ICS. 1 exacerbation = group E Start LABA + LAMA, not LABA/ICS Triple therapy if eosinophils ≥300

source.name: GOLD 2027 Report. Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD.
source.says: Group A should be offered initial bronchodilator treatment (a LAMA, or a short-acting bronchodilator if unavailable). Group B starts LABA+LAMA. Group E starts LABA+LAMA, considering LABA+LAMA+ICS if eosinophils are 300 cells/µL or more.

title: A COPD exacerbation gets a steroid, and antibiotics are selective
lead: A COPD exacerbation is treated with a short systemic steroid. Antibiotics are for increased sputum purulence plus increased dyspnea or volume.
lines: Noninvasive ventilation is for respiratory acidosis, not for every wheeze.
Oxygen is titrated. A high flow that abolishes the drive is the old harm.
The maintenance inhalers are restarted or started before discharge.
Group A: bronchodilator. Group B and group E: LABA plus LAMA. One moderate or severe exacerbation in the past year is group E.

Do not start LABA/ICS alone. Consider triple therapy when eosinophils are at least 300/µL. A flare gets a systemic steroid for about 5 days. Antibiotics if purulence plus more dyspnea or sputum volume.
miss: Giving a 14-day antibiotic to every patient who is a little more short of breath.
diagramAlt: GOLD 2026, who gets ICS. 1 exacerbation = group E Start LABA + LAMA, not LABA/ICS Triple therapy if eosinophils ≥300

source.name: GOLD 2027 Report. Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD.
source.says: For exacerbations, 40 mg prednisone-equivalent daily for 5 days is recommended. Antibiotics are given with at least two of increased dyspnea, fever, sputum volume, and sputum purulence when purulence is one of them, or when ventilation is required.

title: Asthma oxygen starts below 92% and stops by 95%
lead: GINA 2026 does not give oxygen to an adult or adolescent with acute asthma unless the saturation is below 92%. If oxygen is given, the target stays at or under 95%.
lines: The reliever in the preferred track is ICS-formoterol, including during a mild flare.
A systemic steroid is for the severe attack, not for every cough.
Epinephrine is for anaphylaxis, not for ordinary asthma.
No SABA-only plan. Track 1 uses as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol at steps 1–2, and the same inhaler as maintenance from step 3.
miss: Putting a nonrebreather on a talking patient whose saturation is 96%.
diagramAlt: Acute asthma oxygen. No oxygen if saturation ≥92% If given, target ≤95% in adults Preferred reliever: ICS-formoterol

source.name: GINA 2026 Summary Guide for Asthma Management and Prevention.
source.says: In acute asthma, give oxygen when saturation on room air is under 92% and titrate it to a target saturation of 92-95%. The preferred reliever is ICS-formoterol; SABA-only treatment is not recommended.

title: Severe pneumonia uses a beta-lactam plus a macrolide
lead: Severe community-acquired pneumonia is treated with a beta-lactam plus a macrolide, or a beta-lactam plus a fluoroquinolone. One drug is not enough.
lines: Severe pneumonia is combination therapy. MRSA and Pseudomonas coverage is added only for specific risks.
Add MRSA or Pseudomonas coverage only when the risk the guideline names is present.
Blood cultures are for severe disease, not for every walking outpatient.
Outpatient, no comorbidity: amoxicillin or doxycycline. A macrolide alone only where pneumococcal resistance is under 25%.
Severe inpatient disease: beta-lactam plus a macrolide, or beta-lactam plus a respiratory fluoroquinolone. Do not add metronidazole for the word aspiration.
miss: Using an oral macrolide alone for a patient who is in shock.
diagramAlt: Pneumonia: where and which drug. Hypoxia, shock, or confusion: admit Severe: beta-lactam + macrolide No routine anaerobic drug for aspiration

source.name: 2019 ATS/IDSA Guideline for Diagnosis and Treatment of Adults with Community-acquired Pneumonia.
source.says: Combination therapy with a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or a beta-lactam plus a respiratory fluoroquinolone should be the treatment of choice for severe CAP.

title: A stable pulmonary embolus is anticoagulated
lead: A pulmonary embolus with a normal blood pressure is treated with anticoagulation. Systemic thrombolysis is for hypotension or shock.
lines: Start the anticoagulant if the scan will be delayed and the bleeding risk is acceptable.
Right-heart strain with a normal pressure is not an automatic lytic.
A DOAC is appropriate for most stable patients.
Systolic pressure under 90 mm Hg or shock is high-risk and gets reperfusion. A normal pressure gets anticoagulation.
Hemodynamic instability defines high-risk pulmonary embolism and the reperfusion decision. Stable patients are anticoagulated.
miss: Thrombolysing a clot because the CT report said the clot was large.
diagramAlt: Pulmonary embolism split. Hypotension or shock: reperfuse Normal pressure: anticoagulate Right-heart strain alone is not a lytic

source.name: 2026 AHA/ACC/Multisociety Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism in Adults (Guideline-at-a-Glance).
source.says: In PE categories A1-C2 (normotensive), systemic thrombolysis should not be used over anticoagulation alone because of bleeding and intracranial hemorrhage risk. DOACs are recommended over VKAs for patients eligible for oral anticoagulation.

more.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism

title: Hold the SGLT2 inhibitor when the patient is fasting or critically ill
lead: An SGLT2 inhibitor is held for prolonged fasting, surgery, or critical illness because of ketoacidosis. A small early drop in eGFR is not a reason to stop it forever.
lines: Continue it if the eGFR later falls below 20, unless dialysis starts or the patient cannot tolerate it.
The indication includes type 2 diabetes with CKD and eGFR at least 20, and CKD with heart failure or heavy albuminuria.
Restart it when the patient is eating and stable.
miss: Stopping the drug permanently because eGFR fell 4 points in the first month.
diagramAlt: SGLT2 inhibitor rules. Start at eGFR ≥20 if diabetes + CKD Also if HF, or ACR ≥200 mg/g Hold if fasting, surgery, or critical illness

source.name: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease.
source.says: It is reasonable to withhold SGLT2i during prolonged fasting, surgery, or critical medical illness, when people may be at greater risk for ketosis. Once started, continue even if eGFR falls below 20 unless not tolerated or KRT starts.

title: Severe symptoms of hyponatremia get hypertonic saline
lead: A seizure or deep coma from hyponatremia is treated with hypertonic saline now. Fluid restriction is for the stable patient.
lines: US expert panel: 100 mL of 3% saline over 10 minutes, up to three boluses.
European regimen: 150 mL of 3% saline over 20 minutes, repeated up to twice.
Aim for a 4 to 6 mmol/L rise in the first hour, then recheck.
Stop if the 24-hour rise will pass 10 mmol/L. That is the osmotic demyelination risk.
miss: Over-correcting by more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours, which risks osmotic demyelination.
diagramAlt: Severely symptomatic hyponatremia. US: 100 mL 3% over 10 min, up to x3 EU: 150 mL over 20 min, repeat x2 First hour: rise of 4-6 mmol/L Over 10 mmol/L in 24 h risks ODS

source.name: European clinical practice guideline on diagnosis and treatment of hyponatraemia (ESE/ESICM/ERA-EDTA).
source.says: Severe symptoms: prompt IV infusion of 150 mL 3% hypertonic saline over 20 minutes, repeated twice or until a 5 mmol/L rise. Limit the rise to 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours and 8 mmol/L every 24 hours thereafter.

more.name: US expert panel recommendations on hyponatremia (Verbalis 2013)

title: Central diabetes insipidus answers to desmopressin
lead: If desmopressin concentrates the urine, the diabetes insipidus is central and desmopressin is the treatment. If it does not, the kidney is the problem.
lines: Nephrogenic disease from lithium is not fixed by more desmopressin.
The patient must be allowed to drink, or you replace the water.
A low sodium means you gave too much desmopressin or the patient drank past it.
miss: Restricting free water in a hypernatremic patient whose urine is already water.

source.name: StatPearls. Arginine Vasopressin Disorder (Diabetes Insipidus).
source.says: After water deprivation, desmopressin increases urine osmolality by more than 100% in complete central DI and up to 50% in partial central DI. In adults, nephrogenic (AVP-resistance) disease is mostly from chronic lithium or hypercalcemia.

title: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis is the hyperkalemic one
lead: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis raises potassium. It is low aldosterone effect, often from diabetes or from a drug that blocks that axis.
lines: Stop the offending drug when you can: a potassium-sparing diuretic, an NSAID, or sometimes the ACE inhibitor if the potassium is dangerous.
Type 1 and type 2 waste potassium. Do not treat them as type 4.
Fludrocortisone is a selected treatment, not the first reflex.
miss: Giving more spironolactone for the blood pressure while the potassium is 6.2.

source.name: StatPearls. Renal Tubular Acidosis.
source.says: Type 4 hyperkalemic RTA is the most common type; its main causes are diabetic nephropathy with hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism and urinary tract obstruction. Fludrocortisone treats the hyperkalemia but is not usually used because it can worsen hypertension, heart failure, and edema.

title: Saline-responsive alkalosis gets chloride
lead: A metabolic alkalosis with a low urine chloride is treated with saline and potassium. A high urine chloride is mineralocorticoid excess and saline will not fix it.
lines: Vomiting and a remote diuretic are the low-chloride stories.
Active diuretic use can look high-chloride. The history matters.
Acetazolamide is a selected option when the patient cannot take volume, not the first bag.
Saline will not fix hyperaldosteronism. Potassium is low in both and is replaced.
miss: Pouring saline into primary hyperaldosteronism.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Metabolic Alkalosis.
source.says: Chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis has urine chloride under 10 mEq/L and is treated by repleting chloride, potassium, and fluid; chloride-resistant alkalosis (urine chloride over 20 mEq/L) is treated by addressing the cause, such as aldosterone excess.

title: Ventilate the patient whose CO2 is rising
lead: A rising PaCO2 with a falling pH is treated by ventilation. Oxygen does not remove CO2.
lines: Noninvasive ventilation is the first step when the patient can protect the airway and is not in shock.
A chronic retainer is not driven to a CO2 of 40 in an hour.
Sedation that is still running is a cause you can stop.
miss: Increasing the oxygen liter flow as the only response to a CO2 of 80 and a pH of 7.18.
diagramAlt: When to start NIV. COPD flare with low pH and high CO2 Patient must protect the airway Oxygen alone does not clear CO2

source.name: GOLD 2027 Report. Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD.
source.says: NIV is the initial mode of ventilation for acute respiratory failure in COPD exacerbations; it improves acute respiratory acidosis, increasing pH and decreasing PaCO2, and reduces mortality and intubation rates.

more.name: Official ERS/ATS clinical practice guidelines: noninvasive ventilation for acute respiratory failure (2017)

title: Tension pneumothorax shifts the mediastinum
lead: Tension pneumothorax is a one-way leak that transmits pressure to the mediastinum and shifts the trachea away from the silent side.
lines: The trachea moves away from the side of the tension.
A simple pneumothorax in a stable patient can wait for the image.
Neck veins are up because venous return is blocked, not because the heart is failing.
miss: Sending a crashing patient to radiology for a two-view film.

source.name: StatPearls. Tension Pneumothorax.
source.says: Tension pneumothorax is intrapleural air under pressure causing lung collapse and mediastinal shift; diagnosis is clinical, with hypotension, unilateral breath sounds, distended neck veins, and tracheal deviation.

title: ARDS tidal volume is predicted body weight
lead: Ventilate the acute respiratory distress syndrome at about 6 mL per kilogram of predicted body weight, and keep the plateau pressure at or under 30.
lines: Predicted weight comes from height and sex, not from the scale.
Chasing a normal CO2 with big breaths injures the lung.
Fluids are conservative once shock has been resuscitated.
Bilateral infiltrates not explained by left-atrial pressure. Tidal volume 6 mL/kg predicted body weight from height and sex.
miss: Setting 12 mL per kilogram of actual weight because the saturation looks better.
diagramAlt: ARDS tidal volume. 6 mL/kg predicted body weight Use height and sex, not the scale Plateau pressure ≤30 cm H2O

source.name: ATS/ESICM/SCCM Clinical Practice Guideline: Mechanical Ventilation in Adult Patients with ARDS (Summary for Clinicians).
source.says: Adults with ARDS should receive mechanical ventilation that limits tidal volumes to 4-8 mL/kg predicted body weight and inspiratory plateau pressure to under 30 cm H2O (strong recommendation).

more.name: ATS 2024 update on management of adult ARDS
ARDSNet ARMA trial (NEJM 2000)

title: Remove the antigen in hypersensitivity pneumonitis
lead: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is treated by removing the bird, the mold, or the farm antigen. A steroid without removal fails.
lines: The history is the test you cannot order.
Acute disease follows exposure by hours.
Chronic scarring will not reverse if the patient goes home to the same bird.
Hours after birds, mold, or a barn. Removing the antigen is required. A steroid without removal fails.
Chronic disease scars the mid and upper lungs. Name the antigen in the discharge instructions.
miss: Adding a steroid and sending the patient back to the pigeon coop.

source.name: ATS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline. Diagnosis of Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis in Adults.
source.says: Patients with nonfibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis who avoid ongoing exposure to the inciting agent may have a favorable prognosis, with possible stabilization or full recovery.

title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is not a prednisone disease
lead: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is treated with an antifibrotic drug and supportive care, not with a long prednisone course as the disease-modifying plan.
lines: Oxygen for hypoxemia and pulmonary rehabilitation are part of care.
Acute worsening is a different event and needs a different evaluation.
Basal, peripheral honeycombing and Velcro crackles. Exclude connective-tissue disease and exposures before calling it idiopathic.
Nintedanib or pirfenidone is the disease-modifying choice. Long-term prednisone is not that treatment.
miss: Prescribing months of high-dose prednisone as the only treatment of honeycombing.
diagramAlt: IPF drug. Nintedanib or pirfenidone Not long-term prednisone as the disease drug Oxygen if hypoxemic

source.name: ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (an update) and Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis in Adults.
source.says: Antifibrotic treatment is indicated for patients diagnosed with IPF; nintedanib and pirfenidone were recommended for IPF in prior guidelines and slow disease progression.

more.name: ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT IPF treatment guideline (2015)

title: Bronchiectasis is cleared, and antibiotics treat the flare
lead: Bronchiectasis is treated with airway clearance every day. Antibiotics treat a flare or a identified organism such as Pseudomonas, not the anatomy.
lines: Find the cause: cystic fibrosis, immunodeficiency, or a prior infection.
A CT that shows the dilation is the diagnosis. A normal film does not exclude it.
Suppressive antibiotics are a specialist decision, not the first inhaler.
CT shows tram tracks and the signet-ring sign. A normal chest film does not exclude it.
miss: Rotating oral antibiotics forever and never teaching clearance.

source.name: ERS clinical practice guideline for the management of adult bronchiectasis.
source.says: Strong recommendations favor airway clearance for most patients, long-term macrolides for those at high exacerbation risk, and long-term inhaled antibiotics with chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection at high exacerbation risk.

title: Correct hypernatremia slowly
lead: Replace the free-water deficit of hypernatremia gradually. A fast drop swells a brain that has made new osmoles.
lines: Let a patient with an intact thirst drink.
Desmopressin is for central diabetes insipidus, not for a patient who simply had no access to water.
Concentrated urine means the kidney is holding water and intake was the problem. Dilute urine is diabetes insipidus.
miss: Dropping the sodium from 162 to 140 overnight with free water.
diagramAlt: Hypernatremia pace. Free-water deficit, replaced slowly Recheck sodium. Do not drop it overnight Desmopressin only if central DI

source.name: StatPearls. Hypernatremia.
source.says: Hypernatremia is corrected by calculating the free water deficit, replaced over 48 to 72 hours with a fall in serum sodium not exceeding 0.5 mEq per hour, with close monitoring of correction rate, urine output, and ongoing losses.

title: Hypokalemia severity is graded from the serum value
lead: Mild hypokalemia is 3 to 3.4 mmol/L and moderate is 2.5 to 3. The serum value is not the body's whole store.
lines: A serum potassium of about 3.5 mmol/L is the lower limit of normal in this chapter.
3 to 3.4 mmol/L is mild, 2.5 to 3 is moderate, and under 2.5 mmol/L is severe.
Weakness, cramps, and palpitations follow the severity. Arrhythmia is the severe risk.
The serum value is a small fraction of body stores, so it does not measure total potassium.
miss: Calling a potassium of 2.4 mmol/L mild, or judging total body stores from the serum value alone.
diagramAlt: Hypokalemia severity. Floor about 3.5 mmol/L Mild 3 to 3.4; moderate 2.5 to 3 Severe: under 2.5 mmol/L

source.name: StatPearls. Hypokalemia.
source.says: An acceptable lower limit of normal serum potassium is 3.5 mmol/L. A level of 2.5 to 3 mmol/L is moderate, and below 2.5 mmol/L is severe hypokalemia.

title: Symptomatic hypocalcemia gets calcium
lead: A seizure, tetany, or a long QT from hypocalcemia gets intravenous calcium. Asymptomatic mild hypocalcemia is oral and a search for the cause.
lines: Check magnesium. A low magnesium keeps calcium low.
After thyroid surgery, watch the calcium for the first day.
Correct the albumin before you call a total calcium low.
Prolonged QT, Chvostek or Trousseau sign, tetany, or a seizure gets intravenous calcium. Recheck magnesium.
miss: Giving a bolus of calcium for a mildly low total calcium in a comfortable patient with a low albumin.
diagramAlt: Symptomatic hypocalcemia. Long QT, tetany, or seizure: IV calcium Check magnesium with it Post-thyroidectomy: scheduled calcium checks

source.name: Society for Endocrinology Emergency Endocrine Guidance: Emergency management of acute hypocalcaemia in adult patients.
source.says: Severe hypocalcaemia (under 1.9 mmol/L and/or symptomatic) is a medical emergency: give 10-20 mL 10% calcium gluconate IV over 10 minutes with ECG monitoring, repeated until asymptomatic, then a calcium gluconate infusion.

title: Adult polycystic kidney disease: treat the pressure and the headache
lead: Hypertension in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease is treated. A sudden severe headache is an aneurysm until imaged.
lines: The kidneys are not biopsied to make this diagnosis.
Tolvaptan is a selected drug that slows growth in the right patient, with a liver-test cost.
Family screening is a conversation, not a surprise CT of every relative.
Autosomal dominant disease: bilateral cysts, hypertension, and intracranial aneurysms. Do not biopsy to diagnose it.
A thunderclap headache is imaged the same day. Autosomal recessive disease is the infantile form with congenital hepatic fibrosis.
miss: Ignoring a thunderclap headache because the patient's usual problem is the kidney.

source.name: StatPearls. Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
source.says: Tolvaptan slows ADPKD progression by blocking vasopressin signaling at the V2 receptor. Blood pressure is treated, with a HALT-PKD target under 120-125/80 mm Hg, and lower targets in preserved GFR.

more.name: KDIGO 2025 Clinical Practice Guideline for ADPKD

title: Alkalinize a uric acid stone
lead: Uric acid stones dissolve when the urine is made less acidic. A plain film that is clear does not mean the stone is gone.
lines: CT or ultrasound sees the stone the film missed.
Allopurinol is for the uric acid production, not the acute colic.
Pain control and a strainer still happen.
Plain films miss uric acid stones.
Allopurinol is not the acute pain drug.
miss: Telling the patient the stone passed because the abdominal film is blank.

source.name: StatPearls. Uric Acid Nephrolithiasis.
source.says: Uric acid stones are radiolucent. Almost two-thirds can be dissolved by increasing urinary pH and volume and lowering hyperuricosuria; potassium citrate is usually the preferred alkalinizing agent.

more.name: AUA guideline: Medical Management of Kidney Stones

title: Bind phosphate with the meal
lead: A phosphate binder is taken with food. A binder swallowed on an empty stomach does not bind the meal the patient is about to eat.
lines: Secondary hyperparathyroidism is treated by lowering phosphate and replacing the vitamin D the kidney no longer activates, in the order the labs demand.
Calcium-based binders add a calcium load. Watch the product.
Dialysis does not excuse the binder.
Phosphate rises, active vitamin D falls, PTH rises. Binders are taken with meals. A bedtime-only dose binds nothing.
miss: Prescribing the binder at bedtime, away from meals.
diagramAlt: Phosphate binder timing. Swallow with the meal Bedtime-only dosing binds nothing Watch the calcium-phosphate product

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD).
source.says: For persistently high serum phosphate despite dietary restriction, phosphate binders taken with meals are recommended; patients should understand the binder types and the importance of taking them with meals.

title: A young woman with fibromuscular stenosis may benefit from opening the artery
lead: Fibromuscular dysplasia of a renal artery in a young woman is the stenosis that is often opened. An older atherosclerotic stenosis is not automatically stented.
lines: An ACE inhibitor can drop the filtration when the whole renal mass sits behind a stenosis.
Recheck the creatinine after you start it.
A bruit is a clue, not a diagnosis.
An ACE inhibitor can drop GFR when both kidneys, or a single kidney, depend on the stenosis. Recheck creatinine within days.
miss: Stenting every atherosclerotic renal artery because the pressure is high.

source.name: StatPearls. Renal Artery Stenosis.
source.says: Fibromuscular dysplasia responds more favorably to angioplasty than atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis, and these patients do not require stenting.

title: Gas in a diabetic kidney is not oral antibiotics
lead: Emphysematous pyelonephritis is treated with antibiotics and a plan to drain or remove the source. It is not a three-day outpatient prescription.
lines: The patient is usually diabetic.
Imaging shows the gas.
A simple pyelonephritis has no gas and can be outpatient if the patient can drink and is not septic.
Gas in the kidney on CT in a diabetic patient is a necrotizing infection, usually E. coli or another gram-negative rod.
Intravenous antibiotics and drainage or nephrectomy. Oral ciprofloxacin and discharge is the miss.
miss: Discharging a febrile diabetic with gas around the kidney on ciprofloxacin.

source.name: StatPearls. Emphysematous Pyelonephritis.
source.says: Diabetes mellitus is found in over 90% of patients with emphysematous pyelonephritis, with mortality of 40% to 90%; care combines antimicrobial therapy with percutaneous drainage or surgical intervention.

title: Minimal change disease in a child is a steroid trial
lead: A child with sudden nephrotic syndrome is treated as minimal change disease with steroids unless a red flag demands a biopsy first.
lines: Hematuria that is heavy, a low complement, or an age outside childhood are reasons not to assume it.
The parents are taught to check the urine and the swelling.
Relapse is common and is not failure of the diagnosis.
Steroids are the first treatment unless hematuria, low complement, or an atypical age demands a biopsy.
miss: Biopsying every edematous toddler before a pediatric nephrologist has seen them.

source.name: KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases.
source.says: In childhood nephrotic syndrome, oral glucocorticoids are recommended for 8 or 12 weeks. Prognosis is best predicted by steroid response, so a kidney biopsy is not usually needed at presentation and is reserved for resistance to therapy or an atypical course.

title: Membranous nephropathy: look for the cause and the clot
lead: Adult membranous nephropathy is tested for PLA2R antibody, hepatitis, lupus, and cancer, and the nephrotic syndrome is a clot risk.
lines: Anticoagulation is considered when the albumin is very low and the bleeding risk allows it.
Not every patient needs immediate immunosuppression.
A renal-vein thrombosis is flank pain and a worsening kidney, not just more protein.
miss: Starting high-dose steroids on day one and never testing for hepatitis B.

source.name: KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases.
source.says: Patients with membranous nephropathy should be evaluated for associated conditions regardless of anti-PLA2R status. Prophylactic anticoagulation is used in nephrotic syndrome when thromboembolic risk exceeds the patient-specific bleeding risk; membranous disease carries particularly high risk.

title: Resuscitate the bleed, then scope it
lead: For a stable ulcer bleed without cardiovascular disease, transfuse at a hemoglobin of 7. Scope after resuscitation, within 24 hours.
lines: Two large IVs, a type and screen, and a restrictive transfusion strategy come before the endoscopy.
High-risk stigmata get endoscopic therapy and a proton-pump inhibitor infusion.
A higher transfusion threshold is reasonable for active cardiovascular disease. The number 7 is not universal.
Without cardiovascular disease, transfuse when hemoglobin is under 7 g/dL. Use a higher threshold, often 8, if coronary disease is active.
miss: Transfusing to a hemoglobin of 10 before the scope, or scoping an unstable patient.
diagramAlt: Ulcer bleed transfusion. No heart disease: transfuse under 7 g/dL Scope after resuscitation, within 24 h Higher threshold if active coronary disease

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline: Upper Gastrointestinal and Ulcer Bleeding.
source.says: For patients hospitalized with UGIB, red cell transfusion at a threshold of 7 g/dL is suggested, and endoscopy is suggested within 24 hours. Endoscopic therapy is recommended for active spurting, oozing, or nonbleeding visible vessels, followed by high-dose PPI for 3 days.

title: Tap the new ascites
lead: New ascites gets a diagnostic tap. A SAAG of 1.1 or more means portal hypertension. A neutrophil count of 250 or more means spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.
lines: Send the cell count, albumin, protein, and culture inoculated at the bedside.
Do not wait for the culture to start antibiotics when the neutrophil count is already at least 250.
For a tap that removes more than 5 liters, give albumin, about 6 to 8 g per liter removed.
miss: Sending the patient home on a higher diuretic dose without tapping new or painful ascites.
diagramAlt: Ascites tap. SAAG ≥1.1: portal hypertension Neutrophils ≥250: treat SBP now Remove >5 L: albumin 6–8 g per liter

source.name: AASLD Practice Guidance: Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Management of Ascites, Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis and Hepatorenal Syndrome.
source.says: A diagnostic paracentesis should be performed in all patients with new-onset ascites. A SAAG of 1.1 g/dL or more is highly suggestive of portal hypertension. IV antibiotics are started empirically, before culture results, when ascitic PMN count exceeds 250/mm3. Albumin 6-8 g per liter removed is given for paracentesis over 5 L.

title: The two ulcer causes are H. pylori and NSAIDs
lead: A peptic ulcer is Helicobacter pylori or an NSAID until a rarer cause is proved. The pain’s relation to meals is not reliable enough to locate it.
lines: A clean-based ulcer that has stopped bleeding does not need a heroic transfusion target.
Alarm features, including bleeding, weight loss, and age, get an endoscopy.
Test and treat Helicobacter pylori with a full eradication regimen, then a test of cure. A proton-pump inhibitor alone does not eradicate.
miss: Locating the ulcer from whether food helps, and never testing for H. pylori.
diagramAlt: H. pylori. Full eradication regimen Test of cure after antibiotics PPI alone does not eradicate

source.name: StatPearls. Peptic Ulcer Disease.
source.says: Helicobacter pylori-associated and NSAID-associated disease account for the majority of peptic ulcer disease. A test after treatment can confirm eradication 4 to 6 weeks after stopping therapy.

title: Reflux is a sphincter that relaxes, not a weak swallow
lead: Gastroesophageal reflux is transient relaxation of the lower sphincter. Dysphagia, bleeding, or weight loss is an alarm, not simple reflux.
lines: A trial of acid suppression is reasonable when the story is heartburn and there is no alarm.
An alarm symptom gets an endoscopy, not a longer antacid trial.
Weight loss and a head of the bed are part of the treatment, not decorations.
Typical heartburn can start with an 8-week proton-pump inhibitor trial. Alarm features — dysphagia, bleeding, anemia, or weight loss — are an endoscopy.
A bird-beak esophagus that does not relax is achalasia, not a failed acid drug. Manometry, not another month of a PPI, is the next test.
miss: Refilling a proton-pump inhibitor for progressive dysphagia.

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease.
source.says: For classic heartburn and regurgitation without alarm symptoms, an 8-week trial of empiric once-daily PPI before a meal is recommended. Alarm symptoms such as dysphagia, weight loss, bleeding, vomiting, or anemia call for endoscopy as soon as feasible.

title: Pancreatitis is lipase, gallstones, and alcohol
lead: Acute pancreatitis is epigastric pain to the back with a lipase at least three times normal. Gallstones and alcohol are the two causes to name first.
lines: Two of three: typical pain, lipase at least three times the upper limit, and imaging only if the diagnosis is unclear.
Early fluid is the treatment. Feed when pain allows. Do not trend the lipase every morning.
Antibiotics are not routine for uncomplicated pancreatitis.
miss: Starving the patient for a week because the lipase was high on day one.

source.name: American College of Gastroenterology Guidelines: Management of Acute Pancreatitis.
source.says: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed by 2 of 3: typical pain, amylase or lipase over 3 times the upper limit, and characteristic imaging. Gallstones (40%-70%) and alcohol (25%-35%) are the most common causes. Early oral feeding is suggested in mild disease; prophylactic antibiotics are not suggested even in severe disease.

title: Small-bowel obstruction stacks air-fluid levels
lead: Small-bowel obstruction is vomiting, distension, and air-fluid levels. Prior surgery means adhesions until a hernia or a mass is found.
lines: A closed loop and a fever or a lactate that is rising is ischemia. That patient does not wait.
Nasogastric suction and fluids are the first orders for a stable partial obstruction.
Complete obstruction with peritonitis is an operation.
Adhesions after surgery are the common cause. Nasogastric suction and fluids if the patient is stable and there is no peritonitis.
miss: Watching a febrile, acidotic obstruction overnight because the last one was adhesions.

source.name: Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO): 2017 update of the evidence-based guidelines from the WSES.
source.says: Non-operative management should always be tried in adhesive small bowel obstruction unless there are signs of peritonitis, strangulation, or bowel ischemia; it includes fluid resuscitation, electrolyte correction, nutritional support, and prevention of aspiration.

more.name: StatPearls. Small Bowel Obstruction.

title: Mesenteric ischemia hurts more than the exam shows
lead: Acute mesenteric ischemia is pain out of proportion to the exam. Atrial fibrillation or a low-flow state is the setup, and lactate is late.
lines: The embolus prefers the superior mesenteric artery.
A soft abdomen does not reassure you. The abdomen becomes hard when the bowel is already dead.
CT angiography is the test. A plain film is not.
Pain with a soft abdomen, often atrial fibrillation or low flow. Lactate rises after bowel is injured.
CT angiography and a surgeon now. Heparin if the working diagnosis is embolus and the patient is not bleeding.
miss: Waiting for the lactate or the rigid abdomen before calling the surgeon.

source.name: Acute mesenteric ischemia: updated guidelines of the World Society of Emergency Surgery.
source.says: Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to physical findings should be assumed to be acute mesenteric ischemia until disproven. CTA should be performed without delay, even with acute kidney injury. Lactate alone does not reliably separate early from irreversible ischemia.

title: Cholecystitis is a blocked cystic duct
lead: Acute cholecystitis is a stone blocking the cystic duct. The pain is right-upper-quadrant and Murphy's sign stops the breath.
lines: Fever and a high white count mark inflammation, not just biliary colic.
Ultrasound shows the wall, the stone, and the fluid.
Early surgery is the treatment of uncomplicated disease. Antibiotics alone do not remove the stone.
Jaundice means the stone may be in the duct. That is a different drainage than removing the gallbladder alone.
miss: Diagnosing cholangitis, which adds jaundice and needs a drained duct, from an isolated gallbladder.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Cholecystitis.
source.says: Acute cholecystitis is most often caused by gallstone obstruction of the cystic duct. For appropriate surgical candidates, early laparoscopic cholecystectomy during the initial hospitalization remains the preferred approach.

title: Achalasia is opened or injected, not suppressed with acid medicine
lead: Achalasia is treated by disrupting the lower sphincter: dilation, surgery, or an endoscopic myotomy. A proton-pump inhibitor does not relax it.
lines: Manometry confirms the diagnosis.
Endoscopy excludes a cancer at the junction that mimics the beak.
Aspiration at night is why the treatment is not optional.
Failure of LES relaxation and absent peristalsis. Bird-beak barium. Manometry confirms. Endoscopy excludes a cancer mimic.
miss: Refilling a proton-pump inhibitor for regurgitation of undigested food.

source.name: ACG Clinical Guidelines: Diagnosis and Management of Achalasia.
source.says: Esophageal pressure topography (high-resolution manometry) is recommended for diagnosis. Disruptive LES therapy is the treatment: laparoscopic Heller myotomy over botulinum toxin in surgical candidates, pneumatic dilation over botulinum toxin, and POEM or myotomy for type III.

title: Celiac disease is a gluten-free diet, after the test
lead: Celiac disease is treated by removing gluten. Do the serology and, when needed, the biopsy before the diet, or the tests go negative.
lines: Check total IgA or the test lies.
Dermatitis herpetiformis is the same diet.
A first-degree relative with symptoms is tested. A gene test alone is not the diagnosis.
Order IgA tissue transglutaminase and a total IgA while the patient is still eating gluten. A gluten-free week before the test can make it falsely negative.
HLA-DQ2 or DQ8 is necessary and not sufficient. Adults with a positive serology still need the biopsy before the diet is declared the treatment.
miss: Starting a gluten-free diet the week before the endoscopy.

source.name: ACG Clinical Guidelines Update: Diagnosis and Management of Celiac Disease.
source.says: EGD with multiple duodenal biopsies is recommended to confirm the diagnosis in children and adults. Case finding is recommended; in IgA deficiency, testing uses IgG-based antibodies. Treatment is a gluten-free diet aimed at intestinal healing.

title: Severe ulcerative colitis is managed from the current ACG guideline
lead: Severe ulcerative colitis is admitted for steroids and for a watch on toxic megacolon. Antidiarrheals and opioids are stopped.
lines: The 2025 ACG update is the current practice guideline for ulcerative colitis in adults.
A systemically ill patient is assessed under that guideline rather than continued on an unchanged outpatient plan.
Admit, start an intravenous steroid, stop loperamide and opioids, and test for C. difficile. Toxic megacolon is a surgical call.
miss: Sending a systemically ill patient with ulcerative colitis home to continue the outpatient plan.
diagramAlt: Severe ulcerative colitis. Admit. IV steroid Stop loperamide and opioids C. difficile test. Megacolon: call surgery

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline Update: Ulcerative Colitis in Adults.
source.says: In acute severe UC, give methylprednisolone 60 mg/day or hydrocortisone 100 mg 3-4 times daily, test initially for C. difficile, and avoid NSAIDs, narcotics, and anticholinergic drugs. Failure of IV steroids by 3 days calls for infliximab or cyclosporine rescue.

title: Chronic pancreatitis enzymes are taken with the meal
lead: Pancreatic enzymes are swallowed with food. A capsule at bedtime does not treat the steatorrhea of the meal.
lines: Diabetes from lost islets is treated as diabetes.
Alcohol is stopped. That is the disease-modifying act.
A new jaundice is cancer until imaged, not more enzymes.
Fecal elastase is low. Enzymes are taken with every meal and snack, not at bedtime alone.
miss: Prescribing the enzymes once daily on an empty stomach.

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Pancreatitis.
source.says: Pancreatic enzyme supplementation is typically taken with meals.

title: Varices bleed: drug, antibiotic, band
lead: Suspected variceal bleeding gets a vasoactive drug such as octreotide, an intravenous antibiotic, and urgent endoscopy for banding.
lines: Resuscitate, but do not flood the patient into a higher portal pressure.
Intubation for a massive hematemesis protects the airway before the scope.
Acute variceal bleeding is treated with a vasoactive drug, an antibiotic, and endoscopic therapy. A nonselective beta blocker is prevention after hemostasis, not the treatment of shock.
miss: Starting propranolol while the pressure is 80 and the patient is still vomiting blood.
diagramAlt: Variceal bleed. Octreotide + IV antibiotic Band. Do not start a beta blocker in shock Beta blocker is secondary prevention later

source.name: AASLD Practice Guidance on risk stratification and management of portal hypertension and varices in cirrhosis.
source.says: Suspected variceal bleeding is managed with resuscitation, a conservative transfusion strategy, and prompt vasoactive therapy and antimicrobial prophylaxis, with endoscopic evaluation within 12 hours. Without TIPS, a nonselective beta blocker starts when vasoactive therapy stops.

title: Chronic hypertension in pregnancy starts at 140/90
lead: Treat chronic hypertension in pregnancy at 140/90. Do not wait for 160/110.
lines: This is the CHAP threshold ACOG adopted. It is a threshold to treat, not a proved ideal target below 140/90.
Continue an effective agent that is safe in pregnancy. Labetalol, nifedipine, and hydralazine are the usual choices.
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and a statin stay stopped.
Treat at 140/90. Labetalol and nifedipine are the usual agents. Stop ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and statins.
miss: Stopping the patient's amlodipine-class plan and watching until the pressure is severe. The error is the wait, and also keeping an ACE inhibitor.
diagramAlt: Blood pressure in pregnancy. Chronic HTN: treat at 140/90 Severe: 160 or 110, treat within minutes Magnesium prevents seizures. It is not the BP drug

source.name: ACOG Practice Advisory. Chronic Hypertension and Pregnancy (CHAP).
source.says: ACOG recommends 140/90 mm Hg as the threshold to start or titrate treatment for chronic hypertension in pregnancy.

title: Severe hypertension in pregnancy is treated now
lead: A sustained pressure of 160 systolic or 110 diastolic in pregnancy or postpartum is treated promptly. Magnesium is for the seizure risk, not for the pressure.
lines: Confirm a severe value and treat. Do not wait four hours, and do not wait for the labs.
IV labetalol, IV hydralazine, or immediate-release oral nifedipine are the acute drugs.
Magnesium sulfate prevents the seizure. It is given with the antihypertensive, not instead of it.
Severe-range blood pressure is treated urgently. Magnesium sulfate is seizure prophylaxis in preeclampsia with severe features.
miss: Starting magnesium and leaving a pressure of 180/115 untreated while the labs are pending.
diagramAlt: Blood pressure in pregnancy. Chronic HTN: treat at 140/90 Severe: 160 or 110, treat within minutes Magnesium prevents seizures. It is not the BP drug

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia.
source.says: Severe-range blood pressure is treated urgently. Magnesium sulfate is seizure prophylaxis in preeclampsia with severe features, which is the recommendation in ACOG Practice Bulletin. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia.

title: Who gets aspirin to prevent preeclampsia
lead: High-risk patients start low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks to lower the risk of preeclampsia.
lines: High risk includes prior preeclampsia, a multifetal pregnancy, chronic hypertension, diabetes, kidney disease, and autoimmune disease.
The dose used in the recommendation is 81 mg daily.
Aspirin does not treat a pressure of 170. That pressure gets an antihypertensive and, if severe features are present, magnesium.
miss: Saving the aspirin for the third trimester, or offering it as the treatment of a pressure of 170/110.

source.name: USPSTF. Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality.
source.says: Low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks is recommended for pregnant people at high risk of preeclampsia.

title: Give insulin in DKA until the gap closes
lead: In diabetic ketoacidosis, continue insulin after the glucose falls and add dextrose. Stop insulin when the gap has closed and the patient is eating, not when the glucose first looks pretty.
lines: The 2024 hyperglycemic-crisis guidance is fluids, potassium, and insulin, and bicarbonate is not routine.
An SGLT2 inhibitor can cause ketoacidosis with a glucose that is not very high. Ask about the drug.
Anion-gap acidosis and ketones. If potassium is under 3.3 mEq/L, replace it before insulin, because insulin will drop the serum potassium.
miss: Turning off the insulin drip because the glucose reached 180 while the bicarbonate is still 10.
diagramAlt: DKA order. Fluid first K under 3.3: replace K before insulin Keep insulin on; add dextrose as glucose falls

source.name: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report.
source.says: Insulin continues until ketoacidosis resolves. Dextrose is added when glucose falls so the insulin can keep running.

title: Thyroid storm: PTU, then iodide an hour later
lead: Thyroid storm treatment starts with propylthiouracil, not iodide. Iodide waits at least 1 hour, a beta blocker and a glucocorticoid are added, and aspirin is avoided. A Burch-Wartofsky score of 45 or more supports the call.
lines: Propylthiouracil is the thionamide preferred in storm because it also blocks conversion of T4 to T3.
Give iodide at least 1 hour after the thionamide. Iodide first supplies substrate for more hormone.
Add a beta blocker and a glucocorticoid. Cool with acetaminophen, not aspirin.
A score of 45 or more supports the diagnosis. A beta blocker alone is not the regimen.
miss: Giving iodide before the thionamide, or using aspirin for the fever.
diagramAlt: Thyroid storm sequence. PTU first. Iodide at least 1 hour later Beta blocker and a glucocorticoid BWPS >=45. No aspirin

source.name: 2016 American Thyroid Association guideline for hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis.
source.says: Thyroid storm, including a Burch-Wartofsky score of 45 or higher, is treated with a beta blocker, propylthiouracil, iodide given at least 1 hour after the thionamide, and a glucocorticoid. Aspirin is avoided.

title: Adrenal crisis is steroid and saline, before the stim test
lead: Adrenal crisis is hydrocortisone and saline now. A cosyntropin test can wait until the patient is alive.
lines: Crisis dose: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV now, then 200 mg over the next 24 hours, with saline.
Do not wait for a corticotropin stimulation test. Recommendation 4.1 treats the unstable patient first.
After recovery, adult maintenance is hydrocortisone 15 to 25 mg a day in divided doses plus fludrocortisone about 0.1 mg.
Send the patient out with stress-dose teaching and a parenteral glucocorticoid for the next emergency.
miss: Holding the glucocorticoid until a stimulation test is finished in an unstable patient.

source.name: Endocrine Society guideline. Primary adrenal insufficiency.
source.says: Recommendation 4.1: adrenal crisis is hydrocortisone 100 mg IV, then 200 mg over 24 hours, plus saline. Do not delay that dose for a corticotropin test. Later maintenance is hydrocortisone 15 to 25 mg a day.

title: Preoperative blockade comes before pheochromocytoma surgery
lead: Prepare a pheochromocytoma with an alpha blocker until the patient is volume-replete, and only then add a beta blocker.
lines: Screen with plasma free metanephrines or urinary fractionated metanephrines. A positive result is followed up, not ignored.
Every patient with a functional tumor gets preoperative blockade before surgery.
Preparation includes a high-sodium diet and a high fluid intake so the blood pressure does not collapse after the tumor is removed.
Block the tumor before incision and load salt and volume so the pressure does not collapse after removal.
miss: Taking a functional pheochromocytoma to surgery without preoperative blockade and volume preparation.

source.name: Endocrine Society guideline. Pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
source.says: All patients with a functional pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma should have preoperative blockade. Preparation includes a high-sodium diet and fluid intake to prevent postoperative hypotension.

title: Pick the diabetes drug for the disease, not the A1C
lead: In type 2 diabetes, start an SGLT2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 receptor agonist with proven benefit for heart failure, kidney disease, or atherosclerotic disease even when the A1C is already at goal.
lines: Heart failure gets an SGLT2 inhibitor.
Atherosclerotic disease can get a GLP-1 receptor agonist, an SGLT2 inhibitor, or both.
Do not wait through a failed metformin trial when one of those diseases is already present.
Chronic kidney disease is its own reason to choose an SGLT2 inhibitor, even when the A1C is close to goal.
miss: Withholding the drug because the A1C is 6.8.

source.name: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment.
source.says: Agents with proven cardiovascular or kidney benefit are recommended irrespective of A1C when heart failure, chronic kidney disease, or atherosclerotic disease is present.

title: A prolactinoma is a dopamine agonist, after the exclusions
lead: Once pregnancy, hypothyroidism, and drugs are excluded, a prolactinoma is treated with a dopamine agonist.
lines: Cabergoline is the usual drug.
A visual-field cut is an urgent MRI and an urgent treatment, not a routine refill.
Surgery is for the patient who cannot take the drug or whose vision is failing despite it.
Exclude pregnancy, hypothyroidism, and antipsychotics or metoclopramide before calling it a tumor.
A modest elevation with a large mass is stalk effect.
miss: Booking transsphenoidal surgery before a pregnancy test.

source.name: StatPearls. Prolactinoma.
source.says: Hyperprolactinemia is not specific to prolactinoma, and alternative causes such as pregnancy, medications, hypothyroidism, and pituitary stalk effect due to other pituitary tumors should be considered in the differential diagnosis.

title: Endometriosis pain is suppressed, and a large cyst is not
lead: Endometriosis pain is treated with hormonal suppression. A large endometrioma is a surgical lesion, not a longer oral contraceptive alone.
lines: Infertility is managed with the fertility plan, which may not be the same as the pain plan.
NSAIDs help pain and do not treat the implants.
A normal exam does not end the workup of cyclic pain and infertility.
Hormonal suppression treats pain. A cyst of several centimeters is surgical. The fertility plan may differ from the pain plan.
miss: Telling a patient with a 7-centimeter chocolate cyst to try ibuprofen for a year.

source.name: StatPearls. Endometriosis.
source.says: Primary cutaneous endometriosis arises without prior surgery, most frequently affecting the umbilicus, also known as "Villar's nodule." The condition typically manifests as a palpable, discolored skin lesion that may fluctuate in size and symptoms, including pain and bleeding over the affected sites on the skin in response to hormonal changes during the menstrual cycle.

title: A ruptured ectopic pregnancy is an operation
lead: A patient with a positive pregnancy test, an empty uterus, and shock goes to surgery. Methotrexate is for a stable, selected ectopic pregnancy.
lines: The criteria for methotrexate include a low hCG, no fetal heartbeat, and a patient who can return.
Rh status is checked.
A falling hCG still needs a documented plan.
Unstable or ruptured: surgery. Methotrexate only if the patient is stable, the hCG is low, there is no embryonic cardiac activity, and follow-up is certain.
Give anti-D immunoglobulin if the patient is Rh-negative. An empty uterus with a positive test and pain is not a threatened miscarriage until the tube is cleared.
miss: Giving methotrexate in the emergency department to a dizzy patient.
diagramAlt: Ectopic pregnancy. Shock or rupture: operating room Methotrexate only if stable and follow-up is sure Rh-negative: give anti-D

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin. Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy.
source.says: A ruptured or unstable ectopic pregnancy is managed surgically. Methotrexate is reserved for a stable patient who meets criteria and can be followed.

title: Abruption is resuscitation and delivery decisions, not a cervical check
lead: Placental abruption is maternal resuscitation, a fetal monitor, and a delivery decision. Do not perform a digital exam until previa is excluded.
lines: Blood products are ready because the clotting factors are consumed.
A dead fetus and coagulopathy is an urgent delivery.
Painful bleeding is not previa.
Painful bleeding and a uterus that does not relax. Blood can be concealed. Fibrinogen falls and can be the first coagulation test to move.
miss: Checking dilation with a finger as the first act.

source.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 63. Antepartum haemorrhage.
source.says: Placental abruption is painful bleeding and is managed by maternal resuscitation and a prompt delivery decision. Do not perform a digital examination until placenta previa is excluded.

title: Previa is delivered operatively when it covers the cervix
lead: A placenta that covers the cervix is delivered by cesarean. Pelvic rest and a planned date are the outpatient plan after the acute bleed has stopped.
lines: A prior cesarean plus previa raises the chance of placenta accreta. That delivery is planned in a center that can handle it.
The acute bleed is resuscitated like any maternal hemorrhage.
The placenta covers the internal os, so labor and a digital exam can cause hemorrhage. Ultrasound makes the diagnosis.
miss: Inducing labor through a complete previa.

source.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 27a. Placenta praevia and placenta accreta spectrum.
source.says: Diagnose placenta previa with ultrasound and do not perform a digital vaginal examination. Plan cesarean delivery if the placenta still covers the internal os. ACOG Committee Opinion 831 is the US timing document for a medically indicated early delivery.

title: Gestational diabetes is treated to a tight glucose, and the newborn is watched
lead: Gestational diabetes that is not controlled with diet is treated with insulin. The newborn is watched for hypoglycemia.
lines: Gestational diabetes is managed from ACOG Practice Bulletin 190, alongside the current ADA Standards of Care.
After birth, the infant is observed. Maternal glucose has been the fetal fuel.
The mother is retested for diabetes postpartum. Pregnancy treatment is not the end of the diagnosis.
Maternal glucose crosses the placenta and maternal insulin does not. The newborn is hyperinsulinemic, so feed early and check a glucose.
miss: Quoting a glucose cutoff that was not taken from Practice Bulletin 190, or skipping the postpartum retest.
diagramAlt: Infant of a diabetic mother. Glucose crosses. Insulin does not Baby is hyperinsulinemic and can be hypoglycemic Feed early. Check a glucose

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 190. Gestational diabetes mellitus.
source.says: Practice Bulletin 190 is the ACOG management document for gestational diabetes. The PubMed text does not print the diagnostic glucose cutoffs, so this bite does not restate a threshold.

title: Do not combine a nitrate and a PDE-5 inhibitor
lead: If a patient has taken a PDE-5 inhibitor, do not give nitroglycerin. The pressure can collapse.
lines: Ask the question out loud before the first spray.
The wait after sildenafil is longer than after some newer drugs. If you do not know the interval, do not give the nitrate.
Chest pain still gets an ECG and the rest of the ACS plan that is safe.
Sildenafil and a nitrate together can drop systolic pressure profoundly. Ask before the first spray.
If the time of the last dose is unknown, do not give the nitrate. The ECG and aspirin still happen.
miss: Giving the spray because the chest pain protocol says so, without asking.

source.name: ACC/AHA expert consensus. Cardiovascular effects of sildenafil and recommendations for its use.
source.says: Nitrate antianginal agents are an absolute contraindication to sildenafil. Together with nitroglycerin, sildenafil can cause a major drop in blood pressure.

title: BPH is growth in the transition zone
lead: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is proliferation of smooth muscle and epithelial cells in the transition zone. Symptoms become more common with age.
lines: It is a histologic diagnosis, not a nodule and not a rising PSA.
The AUA guideline contains the statements on evaluation and on medical management.
A man with retention, infection, or renal failure is not managed with a sample of one drug.
miss: Promising a man that finasteride will help him urinate tonight.

source.name: AUA guideline. Management of lower urinary tract symptoms from benign prostatic hyperplasia. Part I.
source.says: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is proliferation of smooth muscle and epithelial cells within the prostatic transition zone, and the guideline covers its evaluation and medical management.

title: Acute scrotal pain is imaged promptly
lead: Acute scrotal pain is an emergency. Ultrasound is the first-line imaging test and is not left until the next morning.
lines: The differential overlaps, so the history alone does not separate torsion from infection.
Ultrasound is the established first-line imaging modality for acute scrotal disease.
A study booked for the following day is not a prompt diagnosis.
miss: Booking a Doppler study for the next available slot in the morning.

source.name: ACR Appropriateness Criteria. Acute onset of scrotal pain.
source.says: Acute scrotum is an emergency that needs a prompt diagnosis. Ultrasound is the established first-line imaging modality.

title: Ovarian torsion is detorsed even if flow was seen
lead: Ovarian torsion with a convincing story goes to surgery. A Doppler that shows flow does not cancel the operation.
lines: Detorsion and preservation of the ovary is the goal.
A pregnancy test is done because ectopic pregnancy is the other emergency.
Analgesia is given. Observation overnight of a twisting ovary is not.
The ovary has a dual blood supply, so Doppler flow can be present in a twisted ovary.
miss: Discharging the patient because arterial flow was documented.

source.name: StatPearls. Ovarian Torsion.
source.says: Ovarian torsion is a gynecologic surgical emergency in which the ovary rotates around the ligaments supporting it within the adnexa, partially or completely obstructing its blood supply.

title: Pelvic inflammatory disease treats the patient and the partner
lead: Pelvic inflammatory disease is treated with a regimen that covers gonorrhea and chlamydia, and the partner is treated.
lines: Treat the patient and arrange treatment of sex partners. A prescription for one person is not the regimen.
Cervical motion tenderness is the examination finding that starts that guideline, not a normal Pap smear.
Treat gonorrhea and chlamydia in the patient, and treat the partner in the same plan.
miss: Treating pelvic inflammatory disease without a plan for the partner.
diagramAlt: PID coverage. Cover gonorrhea and chlamydia Treat the partner Abscess that fails antibiotics: drain

source.name: CDC Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021.
source.says: The 2021 CDC STI Treatment Guidelines are the source for treatment of pelvic inflammatory disease, including management of sex partners.

title: The sepsis actions, in order
lead: For suspected sepsis, measure lactate, draw cultures if it does not delay the drug, and give a broad antibiotic. Hypotension or a lactate of 4 or more gets crystalloid.
lines: The Surviving Sepsis hour-1 bundle is those actions plus vasopressors during or after fluid if the patient is still hypotensive, aiming for a mean pressure of 65.
The fluid suggestion for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion is at least 30 mL/kg of IV crystalloid, then reassess. It is not an unmeasured bolus.
A virus swab does not replace the antibiotic while bacterial infection is still possible.
miss: Waiting for the lactate to come back before the antibiotic, or giving a liter and walking away.
diagramAlt: Sepsis hypoperfusion. Lactate, cultures, broad antibiotic At least 30 mL/kg crystalloid if hypoperfused Norepinephrine to MAP 65 if still hypotensive

source.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 Adult Guidelines.
source.says: The hour-1 bundle is lactate, cultures, antibiotics, crystalloid for hypoperfusion, and vasopressors to a mean arterial pressure of 65 when hypotension persists.

title: Epinephrine is the anaphylaxis drug
lead: Anaphylaxis gets intramuscular epinephrine into the mid-outer thigh first. Antihistamines do not treat the airway.
lines: Epinephrine is 0.01 mg/kg, to a maximum of 0.3 mg in children and teenagers and 0.5 mg in adults.
Give epinephrine at the first sign of suspected anaphylaxis.
Draw an acute tryptase as early as possible, ideally within 2 hours of symptom onset. A later baseline is the comparison.
A tryptase under the laboratory cutoff does not exclude anaphylaxis. Many confirmed reactions never cross that line.
miss: Treating anaphylaxis with an antihistamine and quoting a flat 0.3 mg dose for every adult.
diagramAlt: Anaphylaxis dose. Adult: 0.3–0.5 mg of 1 mg/mL IM Mid-outer thigh. Repeat in 5–15 min Watch. Antihistamine is not the treatment

source.name: Anaphylaxis: a 2023 practice parameter update.
source.says: Epinephrine is dosed at 0.01 mg/kg, up to 0.3 mg in children and teenagers and 0.5 mg in adults. Draw an acute tryptase as early as possible, ideally within 2 hours. A tryptase below the laboratory cutoff does not exclude anaphylaxis.

title: Give 100% oxygen for carbon monoxide, and do not trust the pulse oximeter
lead: Carbon monoxide poisoning is treated with 100% oxygen immediately. The pulse oximeter and the PaO2 will look fine.
lines: Suspected carbon monoxide poisoning is an emergency-department decision under the ACEP clinical policy.
Do not clear the patient with a standard pulse oximeter reading. The policy is about measured carboxyhemoglobin and the hyperbaric decision.
Anyone who shared the exposure is assessed. A normal-appearing cohabitant is not proof the air was safe.
Hyperbaric selection follows the policy. A numeric affinity ratio is not the indication.
miss: Discharging a symptomatic patient because the pulse oximeter read normal.
diagramAlt: Carbon monoxide. PaO2 and pulse ox can look normal Content is low. Curve shifts left 100% oxygen now. Whole household

source.name: ACEP clinical policy. Acute carbon monoxide poisoning in the emergency department.
source.says: This ACEP clinical policy addresses emergency evaluation and management of adults with acute carbon monoxide poisoning, including selection for hyperbaric oxygen.

title: Start N-acetylcysteine for a toxic acetaminophen ingestion
lead: A toxic acetaminophen level, or a staggered ingestion you cannot plot, gets N-acetylcysteine. Do not wait for the ALT to rise.
lines: On the treatment line, 150 micrograms per mL at 4 hours is the level that starts acetylcysteine.
Give acetylcysteine within 8 hours of a single acute ingestion when that line is crossed.
The 2023 consensus uses a revised Rumack-Matthew nomogram for a presentation from 4 to 24 hours. A 2-hour level does not clear the patient.
A normal early ALT is not a reason to withhold the antidote.
miss: Waiting past 8 hours, or trusting a 2-hour level, before starting acetylcysteine.
diagramAlt: Acetaminophen antidote. NAPQI uses up glutathione NAC if level is toxic or time is unknown Normal ALT at 2 hours does not clear it

source.name: Management of acetaminophen poisoning in the US and Canada: a consensus statement.
source.says: The treatment line of the Rumack-Matthew nomogram is 150 micrograms per mL at 4 hours, and acetylcysteine is most effective when started within 8 hours. The 2023 consensus uses a revised nomogram for ingestions presenting from 4 to 24 hours.

title: Naloxone wears off before the opioid does
lead: Naloxone reverses opioid apnea and then wears off. The patient is watched, and the dose is repeated or infused.
lines: Support ventilation first if the patient is not breathing. Naloxone does not replace that.
Intravenous naloxone in the AHA poisoning guidance is 0.2 to 2 mg. FDA-labeled nasal spray is 4 mg. Repeat every 2 to 3 minutes.
Titrate to breathing and airway reflexes. A long-acting opioid needs a longer watch because depression returns.
A benzodiazepine taken with the opioid does not delay the naloxone.
miss: One dose of naloxone and a discharge as soon as the patient wakes.
diagramAlt: Naloxone wears off. Opioid half-life is often longer Observe or infuse Methadone and fentanyl outlast one dose

source.name: 2025 AHA Guidelines. Part 10, adult and pediatric special circumstances of resuscitation.
source.says: Part 10 covers opioid overdose. Give naloxone and ventilate; repeat it because respiratory depression can return. The AHA poisoning doses are 0.2 to 2 mg IV and the FDA-labeled nasal spray is 4 mg.

title: Do not give flumazenil to a dependent patient
lead: Benzodiazepine overdose is supported at the airway. Flumazenil is avoided when the patient takes the drug every day or has a seizure history, because it can precipitate a seizure.
lines: A benzodiazepine alone rarely stops breathing the way an opioid does.
Do not give flumazenil to a daily user or in a mixed overdose. It can precipitate a seizure.
If an opioid may be on board, give naloxone. The 2023 update treats naloxone as the safer reversal.
Support the airway while you sort out the mix.
miss: Waking a daily benzodiazepine user with flumazenil and causing a seizure.

source.name: 2023 AHA focused update on cardiac arrest or life-threatening toxicity due to poisoning.
source.says: Isolated benzodiazepine poisoning rarely causes life-threatening hypoventilation. Flumazenil is not routine: it can precipitate seizures in a dependent patient, and naloxone has the better safety profile when an opioid may be present.

title: Alcohol withdrawal is a benzodiazepine titrated to symptoms
lead: Alcohol withdrawal is treated with a benzodiazepine dosed to the tremor, the vital signs, and the confusion. A protocol that front-loads is safer than chasing the next seizure.
lines: Thiamine is given before glucose.
Delirium tremens is a monitored bed.
An antipsychotic alone does not prevent the seizure.
Tremor at about 6–24 hours, seizures at 12–48 hours, delirium tremens at 48–72 hours. Use a symptom-triggered benzodiazepine.
Use a symptom-triggered benzodiazepine for alcohol withdrawal. Give thiamine. An antipsychotic is not the only treatment of withdrawal.
miss: Giving haloperidol as the only drug for a tremulous, tachycardic patient two days after the last drink.
diagramAlt: Alcohol withdrawal orders. Thiamine before glucose Benzodiazepine titrated to symptoms Haloperidol alone does not stop the seizure

source.name: ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management.
source.says: Use a symptom-triggered benzodiazepine for alcohol withdrawal. Give thiamine. An antipsychotic is not the only treatment of withdrawal, which is the recommendation in ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management.

title: Rhabdomyolysis is fluids and a potassium you recheck
lead: Rhabdomyolysis is treated with intravenous fluids. The potassium is rechecked because it can stop the heart before the creatinine rises.
lines: The urine dip lies. Look at the microscope.
Statins and fibrates together are a cause you stop.
Intravenous fluid at a defined rate and a repeat potassium. A tight compartment is opened. Stop the statin.
Dipstick positive for blood and no red cells on microscopy. Potassium can arrest the heart before creatinine rises.
miss: Giving a loop diuretic as the first treatment of tea-colored urine.
diagramAlt: Rhabdomyolysis labs. Dipstick blood, no RBCs on microscope CK in the thousands. K can kill first IV fluid. Open a tight compartment

source.name: StatPearls. Rhabdomyolysis.
source.says: Clinically, rhabdomyolysis can range from mild elevation in creatinine phosphokinase to medical emergencies like compartment syndrome, intravascular fluid depletion, disseminated intravascular coagulation, pigment-induced acute kidney injury (AKI), and cardiac arrhythmias.

title: Dantrolene is the drug for malignant hyperthermia
lead: Malignant hyperthermia is treated by stopping the volatile anesthetic and giving dantrolene. Cooling and hyperventilation come with it.
lines: The CO2 rises first. The temperature follows.
Call for help and the dantrolene cart. Do not keep the vaporizer on.
It is not treated as ordinary intraoperative fever.
This is not neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
miss: Turning up the volatile agent because the patient looks light.
diagramAlt: Malignant hyperthermia. Volatile agent or succinylcholine Rising CO2, then heat and rigidity Stop the gas. Dantrolene. 100% oxygen

source.name: European Malignant Hyperthermia Group guideline. Recognition and management of a malignant hyperthermia crisis.
source.says: Stop the triggering anesthetic and give dantrolene. The first sign is often a rising end-tidal CO2, then rigidity.

title: Fat embolism is supported, not anticoagulated as the only plan
lead: Fat embolism syndrome is treated by supporting the lungs and immobilizing the fracture. Heparin is not the specific antidote.
lines: The timing is one to three days after the long-bone injury.
Petechiae on the chest support the diagnosis and are often absent.
A true venous thrombus can coexist. Do not miss it, and do not call every hypoxic fracture patient a clot.
miss: Starting a heparin drip and cancelling the fixation that would stop the embolization.

source.name: StatPearls. Fat Embolism and Fat Embolism Syndrome.
source.says: Fat embolism and fat embolism syndrome (FES) are clinical phenomena characterized by the systemic dissemination of fat emboli through the circulation.

title: The four screens and the ages
lead: Mammography starts at 40 and is every other year through 74. Colorectal screening starts at 45. Lung screening is annual low-dose CT from 50 to 80 after 20 pack-years.
lines: Cervical screening starts at 21. Ages 21 to 29: cytology every 3 years. Ages 30 to 65: cytology every 3 years, high-risk HPV every 5 years, or both every 5 years.
Stop lung screening after 15 years without smoking, or when a comorbidity limits the benefit.
A family history or a prior high-risk lesion changes the colorectal plan. The age-45 start is for average risk.
miss: Starting mammography at 50, or starting colorectal screening at 50, because that was the old age.
diagramAlt: Screening ages. Breast: every other year from 40 through 74. Colon: start at 45. Lung: yearly low-dose CT from 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years. Cervix: start at 21.

source.name: USPSTF recommendations on breast, colorectal, lung, and cervical cancer screening.
source.says: Breast screening is biennial from 40 through 74 (2024). Colorectal screening starts at 45 (2021). Lung screening is annual low-dose CT from 50 to 80 with a 20 pack-year history (2021). Cervical screening intervals are unchanged from 2018.

title: Screen for depression. Do not swap in a suicide score
lead: Screen adults for depression, including in pregnancy and after birth. A stand-alone suicide-risk questionnaire is an I statement, not a required screen.
lines: A positive depression screen needs a diagnostic interview. The form is not the diagnosis.
Ask about suicide when the interview or the patient's words open that door. That is care, not the population screen the task force declined to endorse.
Treatment follows the diagnosis. A refill of a benzodiazepine is not depression treatment.
Screen adults, including pregnant and postpartum patients, only if someone will diagnose and treat. A positive score is an interview, not an automatic prescription.
miss: Checking a suicide-risk box on every chart and never asking the two depression questions.

source.name: USPSTF. Screening for Depression in Adults. Screening for Suicide Risk.
